docs.title: Sodero Cloud Documentation
docs.text: Build a simulated environment in Studio, configure robot software in Stellar Station, and view the simulation in Theater. Open the portal at app.sodero.io.

docs.title: Start Here
docs.text:
1. Read What Is Sodero Cloud and Key Concepts.
  2. Follow the Quick Start to create, view and stop your first World.
  3. Configure a Robot System when you are ready to connect controllers to simulated robots.

Robot Systems and Robot Worlds use credits from Activate to Deactivate, even while they are stopped (Activate and Run).

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
This manual covers Sodero Cloud. For physical controllers and hardware setup, use the Stellar X manual. The two products run their own releases of Stellar Station, so menus, app versions and document formats can differ (Compatibility).

For help, use Help › Contact support in the portal or contact Sodero.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
• Get started. What Sodero Cloud is, its key concepts, and a Quick Start that creates, runs and stops a Robot World. Example files to connect a Robot System to it.
  • Account, workspaces and projects. Sign-in, workspaces and people, billing and usage, projects, Robot Systems and Robot Worlds, activation, libraries and sharing.
  • Worlds. Build a Robot World in Studio, prepare it for simulation and watch it run in Theater.
  • Robot Systems. Configure Stellar Station in the cloud: apps and packages, the node graph, documents and settings, the connection to the World, and running nodes.
  • Operate robots. Strider, Motion Studio and Articulation with robots in a Robot World.
  • Connect and automate. The Project VPN and AI agents.
  • Reference. Compatibility and Limits and Defaults.

docs.title: Billing and Usage
docs.text: Robot Systems and Robot Worlds use credits while they are active. Credits belong to a workspace. This page explains what uses credits, how to read Billing & Usage, and what happens when credits run out.

docs.title: How Credits Work
docs.text:
• Credits belong to a workspace. Everything active in the workspace's projects uses its balance, whoever activated it, guests and AI agents included.
  • Each workspace has one plan. Your workspace's plan sets how many credits the workspace receives, how many credits per hour each kind of use takes, and the workspace's limits. Billing & Usage shows them.
  • Credits renew every week or every month, depending on the plan, on the workspace's own cycle. Unused plan credits expire at renewal; they do not roll over.
  • Extra credits from Sodero can have their own end date. The credits that expire soonest are used first.

docs.title: What Uses Credits
docs.text:
What Uses credits An active Robot System or Robot World By the hour from Activate to Deactivate, whether or not anything runs in it and whether or not anyone uses it Each Theater viewer and each Studio session While it is open, at your plan's rate for its rendering mode, RTX Real-time or WebGPU The robot cameras of an active World While the cameras are rendered

Billing & Usage shows how many credits each of these uses on your workspace's plan.

Stop is not Deactivate. A stopped Robot System or Robot World is still active and still uses credits. Only Deactivate, or Auto off, ends the use (Activate and Run).

Storage, AI agent tool calls and the Project VPN do not use credits; they count against your plan's limits.

docs.title: The Billing & Usage Dialog
docs.text:
Open the workspace menu and choose Billing & Usage. Everyone in the workspace can open it. It shows the current workspace and updates while it is open. It calls a Robot System a System, a Robot World a World, and the time one of them is active a run.

The top line shows your workspace's plan and, next to Renews, the date of the next renewal. A red Out of credits badge appears when the balance is zero.

docs.title: Credits
docs.text:
Row Meaning credits left The workspace's balance: the plan credits and extra credits that are left Weekly credits or Monthly credits The credits the plan gives the workspace at each renewal Used this week or Used this month Credits used since the last renewal Used in total Credits used since the workspace was created Extra credits from Sodero The extra credits left, each with its end date. Shown only when there are some. Used beyond the balance Credits used after the balance reached zero, on plans that keep running. Shown only when there are some.

Under the rows, a line gives your plan's rates: the credits per hour of a System, of a World and of each kind of renderer.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
Each meter compares what the workspace uses with what the plan allows. The bar turns yellow at 80 % and red when the limit is reached. At the limit, the action that would go over it is refused with a message.

Meter What it counts Projects The workspace's projects. Projects in Trash do not count. Workspace storage Everything stored in the workspace's projects: files, saved versions and project libraries Project libraries The files in the libraries of the workspace's projects Systems and Worlds running at once The Robot Systems and Robot Worlds active right now in the workspace

docs.title: AI Agents and Project VPN This Month
docs.text: AI agent (MCP) tool calls, Project VPN time and Project VPN data count the workspace's use of AI agents and of the Project VPN. They count per calendar month (UTC); the line under them gives the reset date. When the plan also limits tool calls per minute, the line says so: Agents can make up to N tool calls per minute. When a counter reaches its limit, agent tool calls are refused, or Project VPN connections end, until the reset.

docs.title: Recent Runs
docs.text:
The table lists the workspace's recent runs, with the columns Run, Started, Time and Credits. Under each name, the row shows its kind and its project:

Kind What it is System, World A Robot System or Robot World, from Activate to Deactivate World viewer (RTX), World viewer (WebGPU) A Theater viewer World camera renderer The robot cameras of an active World Cosmic Editor (RTX), Cosmic Editor (WebGPU) A Studio session

A row with a green dot is still active and still using credits; its time counts up.

docs.title: When Credits Run Out
docs.text:
What happens at zero depends on your plan. On plans that stop at zero, the rates line ends with When credits run out, runs stop and new runs can't start.

Plan At zero credits Stops at zero The Out of credits badge appears. The workspace's active Robot Systems and Robot Worlds are deactivated, and activating one fails with This workspace has run out of credits. … Keeps running Work goes on. Credits used beyond zero show as Used beyond the balance and are taken from the next credits the workspace receives.

New plan credits arrive at the next renewal. There is no payment page in the portal: to change your workspace's plan or to add credits, contact Sodero.

docs.title: Save Credits
docs.text:
• Deactivate when you are done. A stopped Robot System or Robot World is still active and still uses credits.
  • Keep Auto off on. A Robot System or Robot World that someone forgot then deactivates by itself.
  • Close the views you no longer need. Theater viewers and Studio sessions can use credits while they are open; the rates line shows what each rendering mode uses.
  • Check Recent runs. Rows with a green dot are still using credits.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text: Message What to do This workspace has run out of credits. … Wait for the next renewal, or contact Sodero to add credits. The PLAN plan runs at most N Systems and Worlds at once. … Deactivate a Robot System or Robot World, then activate the new one. Stopping it is not enough. The PLAN plan holds up to N projects in a workspace. … Move a project you no longer need to Trash, or contact Sodero. Also shown when you restore a project from Trash. Not enough workspace storage: … or Not enough room in the project libraries: … The upload does not fit. Delete files you no longer need, or contact Sodero. This workspace's plan doesn't include … The plan has no AI agent tool calls or no Project VPN. Contact Sodero. Limit reached: … for this month. It renews on DATE. The monthly allowance is used up until the date shown.

docs.title: Sign In and Account
docs.text: One Sodero account signs you in to the Sodero Cloud portal at app.sodero.io and to the apps you open from it: Stellar Station, Studio and Theater. This page covers creating the account, signing in, accepting invitations and managing your account.

docs.title: 1. Create an Account
docs.text:
1. Open app.sodero.io and click Create an account under the sign-in form.
  2. Enter your Email and a Password of at least 8 characters, and click Create account.
  3. On Check your email, type the code from Sodero's email and click Verify (Resend code sends a new one). On Email verified, click Continue.
  4. Answer the five profile questions, one per screen, and click Get started. The first question asks for your name, which the people in your workspaces see.

To use your Google account instead, click Continue with Google and choose the account. A new account then answers the profile questions.

Your first workspace. If you do not belong to a workspace yet, Sodero Cloud creates one for you, named after you, with you as its owner (Workspaces and People).

docs.title: 2. Sign In
docs.text:
Open app.sodero.io, enter your Email and Password and click Continue, or click Continue with Google. The portal opens on Projects.

The sign-in screen

docs.title: Reset a Forgotten Password
docs.text:
1. On the sign-in form, click the forgotten-password link under Password.
  2. Enter your Email and click Send code.
  3. Enter the Code from the email and a New password of at least 8 characters, and click Reset password. Then sign in with the new password.

docs.title: First Sign-In to an Account Sodero Set Up for You
docs.text: Sign in with your email address and the temporary password from Sodero's email, if you received one. On Choose a new password, enter a New password (and the Code from the email, if asked) and click Set password.

docs.title: 3. Accept an Invitation
docs.text:
People invite you by email. The email has a Review access button that opens the portal with the invitation.

Invitation to Email subject In the portal A project Sodero project access: NAME Accept invitation (steps below) A Stellar design file Sodero access: NAME Accept invitation or Decline, on a page titled Invite received A workspace Sodero workspace access: NAME Accepted when you open the link while signed in (Join a Workspace from an Invitation)

A Stellar design file is a robot or gateway document saved in Stellar Designer (Make Documents in Stellar Designer).

To accept a project invitation:

  1. In the email, click Review access. Project invite received shows the project, the invited address and who invited you.
  2. If you are not signed in, click Sign in, or Create an account if you are new. Use the address the invitation was sent to. After you sign in, the invitation page comes back.
  3. Click Accept invitation. The portal opens a moment later.

The project appears in Projects if you are a member of its workspace; otherwise it is a guest project. A project invitation has no Decline button: if you do not want to join, ignore the email. Project invitations expire after 7 days.

Message What to do Wrong account You are signed in with another address. Click Sign out, then sign in with the invited address. Invite has expired. Ask for a new invitation. Invite is no longer pending. The invitation was already accepted, declined or cancelled. Invitation not found. The link is incomplete, or the invitation no longer exists. Ask for a new one.

docs.title: 4. Account Settings
docs.text:
Click your avatar at the bottom of the left navigation bar and choose Account Settings.

The Account settings dialog To change Do this Your name Under Basic info, click Edit next to Name, type the name and click Save. Your photo Under Profile, click Change photo, then Upload photo (PNG, JPEG or WebP) or pick a color. Remove goes back to a plain color. Your email address Click Edit next to Email, type the new address and click Save. Then type the code sent to the new address in the Code row and click Confirm. Until then, your account keeps the old address. Emails about Sodero Under Email preferences, turn Product updates & news on or off.

Your name and photo are shown to the people in your workspaces.

Connected AI agents lists the AI agents connected to your account and lets you revoke them (AI Agents).

To change the theme, click your avatar, choose Theme, pick Midnight (dark, the default) or Twilight (light) and click Apply.

docs.title: 5. Sign-In & Security
docs.text:
Click your avatar and choose Sign-in & Security.

Sign-in methods and active sessions Setting What it does Password › Update password Enter your Current password and a New password of at least 8 characters, then click Save. Shown only for accounts that have a password. Google › Connect Lets you also sign in with Continue with Google Google › Disconnect Ends sign-in with Google. Works only when your account has another way to sign in. Sign out everywhere Signs your account out on every device, including this one, without asking first. If you lose a device or think that someone knows your password, use it, then sign in again and update your password.

To sign out of this browser only, click your avatar, choose Sign out and confirm. This also signs you out of the apps you opened from the portal.

docs.title: 6. Delete Your Account
docs.text:
Deleting your account cannot be undone. It also deletes every workspace you own, with all its projects, and every project you created in other people's workspaces, for everyone who works in them.

Deleting your account also removes your profile, your Stellar design files, your memberships, and the Robot Systems and Robot Worlds you created in other people's projects. A workspace you own is deleted with every project in it, including projects that other members created.

Before you delete your account:

  1. Transfer ownership of every workspace that other people still use.
  2. Download local copies of the Robot Systems and Robot Worlds that you or others want to keep.
  3. Deactivate whatever is still active in your workspaces and projects.

Then open Account Settings, click Delete account and confirm with Delete. The portal signs you out. If a message asks you to contact support, part of the deletion did not finish: contact Sodero.

docs.title: Sign-In Messages
docs.text: Message What to do Email or password is incorrect. Check both. If you forgot the password, reset it. Please confirm your email before signing in. Enter the code from the verification email. That code is not correct. … or That code has expired. … Use the code from the most recent email, or ask for a new code. No account uses this email address. Check the address, or create an account. Reset your password to sign in. Reset your password, then sign in with the new one. This account needs an administrator to finish its setup. Contact Sodero. Sign-in didn't finish Google sign-in was cancelled or refused. Click Back to sign in and try again.

docs.title: Workspaces and People
docs.text: A workspace is where a team works together in the Sodero Cloud portal. It holds the team's projects and people, the project libraries, and one plan with its credits (Billing and Usage).

docs.title: The Workspace Menu
docs.text:
You can belong to several workspaces. The portal shows one at a time: its name is at the top left of the page, followed by a badge with your role. Click the name to open the workspace menu.

The workspace menu of Acme Robotics

The menu holds Switch workspace, Create workspace, Workspace settings (owner only), People, Billing & Usage (Billing and Usage) and Leave workspace. Everyone in the workspace can open People and Billing & Usage.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Everyone in a workspace has one role: Owner, Admin or Member. A workspace has exactly one owner. Roles inside a project are separate: see Project Access and Roles.

Action Owner Admin Member Invite people Yes As Member only No Remove people Yes Members only No Change roles, cancel invitations, change workspace settings, transfer ownership, delete the workspace Yes No No Create projects Yes Yes When Members can create projects is on Add, export and delete files in project libraries Yes Yes When Members can manage the Library is on Manage every project in the workspace, Empty all trash Yes Yes No: members have the role they were given in each project

docs.title: 1. Create a Workspace
docs.text: Open the workspace menu, choose Create workspace, enter a name of up to 30 characters and click Create. You are the owner of the new workspace, and the portal switches to it. Each workspace has its own plan and credits.

docs.title: 2. Switch Between Workspaces
docs.text: Open the workspace menu, point at Switch workspace and click a workspace. A check mark shows the current one.

docs.title: 3. Invite People
docs.text:
Owners and admins invite people by email.

  1. Open the workspace menu and choose People.
  2. Under Invite by email, type the person's email address.
  3. Choose the role: Member (the default) or Admin. Only the owner can invite admins.
  4. Click Invite. The invitation is sent at once, without Save.
The People dialog

The person receives an email titled Sodero workspace access: NAME with a Review access button. An invitation is valid for 7 days; inviting the same address again replaces it. The owner sees open invitations in the list, marked Pending. If the dialog says Couldn't send invitation. Try again., check the address; people who are already members cannot be invited.

Tip: To share one project only, invite the person to that project instead (Share and Collaborate).

docs.title: 4. Join a Workspace from an Invitation
docs.text:
1. Sign in with the address the invitation was sent to. If you do not have an account yet, create one with that address first.
  2. While you are signed in, open the invitation email and click Review access. The portal accepts the invitation at once.
  3. Open the workspace menu, point at Switch workspace and choose the new workspace.

If the portal says Invite has expired., ask for a new invitation. If it says You're signed in with a different account. …, sign out, sign in with the address the invitation was sent to and open the link again.

docs.title: 5. Manage Members and Invitations
docs.text:
Open the workspace menu and choose People. Under Members & roles, each person has a row with their name, email address and role.

  • Change a role (owner): choose Admin or Member in the person's role menu.
  • Remove a person: click × on their row. The owner can remove admins and members; admins can remove members.
  • Cancel an invitation (owner): click × on the row of the pending invitation.

Click Save to apply the changes; Cancel discards them. Nobody can change their own role or remove themselves. Members see the list read-only.

docs.title: 6. Change Workspace Settings
docs.text:
Only the owner sees Workspace settings in the workspace menu.

Section What you can do Profile Change color sets the color behind the workspace's initial; Remove resets it. Basic info Edit Name (up to 30 characters) and click Save Permissions Members can create projects, and Members can manage the Library (add, export and delete files in project libraries). Both are off by default.

The color and the permissions are saved as soon as you change them. The dialog also holds Transfer ownership and Delete workspace.

docs.title: 7. Transfer Ownership
docs.text:
1. In Workspace settings, under Ownership, click Transfer ownership. The button stays disabled until someone else has joined the workspace.
  2. Choose the new owner from the members and click Next.
  3. Click Transfer ownership to confirm, then Done.

You become an admin.

docs.title: 8. Delete a Workspace
docs.text:
Deleting a workspace cannot be undone. It permanently deletes every project, file and setting in the workspace, and everyone loses access.

Before you delete a workspace, deactivate its active Robot Systems and Robot Worlds and download local copies of anything you want to keep.

  1. In Workspace settings, under Delete workspace, click Delete workspace.
  2. Type the workspace's exact name and click Delete. The portal opens your next workspace.

docs.title: 9. Leave a Workspace
docs.text:
Open the workspace menu, choose Leave workspace and click Leave. You lose access to the workspace and its projects, except projects you were invited to directly. To come back, someone must invite you again.

The owner cannot leave (You're the only owner of this workspace. Transfer ownership before leaving.): transfer ownership first.

docs.title: Guest Projects
docs.text:
A guest project is a project you were invited to without being a member of its workspace. To see your guest projects, open the workspace menu, point at Switch workspace and choose Guest projects (N), shown when you have some.

In this view, the top bar reads Guest workspace, and Trash and Notifications are hidden. In each project, you have the role you were invited with. Guest projects use the credits of the workspace they belong to.

The left navigation bar, Notifications and the Help menu are described in Find Your Way in the Portal.

docs.title: AI Agents
docs.text:
Connect Claude Code or another AI agent to your Sodero account, then ask it in plain language to work on your projects. The agent reaches Sodero Cloud over the Internet with a sign-in of its own; it needs neither the Project VPN nor anything installed from Sodero.

  • "Which Stations and Worlds in Warehouse Demo are active?"
  • "Activate the warehouse World and the jackal Station, then start them."
  • "Why did a node on jackal stop? Show me its log."

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    You(["You"]) --> Agent["AI agent<br>on your computer"]
    Agent -- "MCP, with its own sign-in" --> Cloud["Sodero Cloud"]
    Cloud --> Projects["The workspaces and projects of your account:<br>Robot Systems, Robot Worlds, files"]
  • You register Sodero once in your agent, as a remote MCP server. The registration belongs to your account, not to one project.
  • The agent signs in through your browser with your Sodero account, and on a consent page you allow it to access your account. It never sees your password, and you can revoke its access at any time.
  • The agent never gets more than your own project roles allow.

docs.title: 1. Register Sodero in Your Agent
docs.text:
Open any project and click AI agents in the top bar. The AI agents (MCP) panel shows the address and ready-made settings for your agent, and what your project role allows.

The AI agents panel of Warehouse Demo Claude CodeOther MCP clients

Click Copy command and run the command once in a terminal:

claude mcp add --transport http --scope user sodero 'https://app.sodero.io/project-access/mcp'

--scope user makes Sodero available in all your working folders.

The client must support remote MCP servers over Streamable HTTP and sign in through your browser (OAuth). Add a remote server with the address that Copy address copies:

https://app.sodero.io/project-access/mcp

For a client with a JSON list of servers, expand Other MCP clients in the panel and click Copy configuration. Don't enter a token or a client ID: the client registers itself and signs in through your browser.

docs.title: 2. Sign In and Allow Access
docs.text:
1. Start the sign-in. In Claude Code, start claude, type /mcp, select sodero and choose Authenticate. Other clients have a Connect or Sign in action.
  2. Your browser opens the Sodero sign-in. Sign in with your Sodero account, not with the account of your AI provider.
  3. The consent page Allow … to connect? shows the permissions the agent requested and says: This agent can access all workspaces and projects available to your account, including those you gain access to later. Current membership and roles always apply. Click Allow access, or Cancel to refuse.
  4. Return to your agent: Sodero is connected.

There is nothing to select: the consent covers your account, and the agent can use every project in which you have a role, now and later. What the agent may do depends on the access its client requests, which the consent page shows:

Requested permissions What the agent may do read project data Read your projects: status, items, files and jobs. This is the access a client gets when it requests no other. read project data and change project data or run commands Also make changes, such as uploading files, activating Stations and Worlds and running the Station and World tools

Approve only your own agent. The consent page shows the name the agent gives itself; Sodero can't verify it. Allow access only right after you started the sign-in from your own agent.

Changes also need a project role that allows them. The project's owner and people with Can manage can change a project through an agent; people with Can view can only read. The AI agents panel of each project says what your role permits there.

A connection lasts up to 30 days. To renew it or change its access, sign the agent in again (in Claude Code, from /mcp), then revoke the entries you no longer need.

docs.title: 3. Tell the Agent Which Project to Use
docs.text: Every request names a project. In the AI agents panel, click Copy project link and paste the link into your request, or give the project's name, for example "List files in Warehouse Demo". When two projects have the same name, use workspace/name.

docs.title: What Agents Can Do
docs.text:
The agent works through Sodero's tools. Each tool name has three parts, for example project.item.start.

Area Tools The agent can Account account.workspace.list, account.project.list List your workspaces, and the projects it may use with read or write permission for each Projects and jobs project.info.get, project.item.list, project.job.list, project.job.status, project.history.list Read a project's Robot Systems and Robot Worlds with their states, its jobs, and the actions agents took in it. Listing the Trash needs Can manage. Run project.item.start, project.item.stop, project.job.start, project.job.cancel Activate or stop up to 8 Stations and Worlds at once, or activate and start them as one job Items project.item.create, project.item.duplicate, project.item.rename, project.item.trash, project.item.restore, project.item.delete_permanently Create, duplicate, rename and trash Robot Systems and Robot Worlds. Restoring and permanently deleting from the Trash need Can manage. Workspaces and projects workspace.project.create, workspace.history.list, project.manage.copy, project.manage.trash Create a project in a workspace where you may create projects, and list those requests. Copying a project and moving it to the Trash need Can manage. Files project.file.list, project.file.download, project.asset.list, project.package.list List and download library files, search the robot and gateway documents of Sodero Assets, and list a Station's apps and packages File changes project.upload.begin, project.upload.finish, project.upload.abort, project.file.rename, project.file.delete Upload files, and rename and delete library files (Usage Limits) Station and World tools system.tools.list, system.tools.describe, system.tools.call Run tools from a catalog of more than 100: Station status and logs, the node graph, documents, Store apps, robot control through Motion Studio, Strider and Articulation, navigation, cameras, and the World

Changes need write access. So does system.tools.call, even for a tool that only reads. Tools for a running Station or World need it to be active.

The agent cannot go beyond your roles, use the Project VPN, read files on your computer through Sodero, or download the contents of Sodero Assets. Cancelling a job stops further steps but doesn't undo changes.

docs.title: Stay in Control
docs.text:
• Approve changes yourself. Most agents can ask before they use a tool. A practical setup: allow the read-only tools freely (account.workspace.list, account.project.list, project.info.get, project.item.list, project.history.list, project.job.list, project.job.status, project.file.list, project.file.download, project.asset.list, project.package.list, workspace.history.list, system.tools.list, system.tools.describe) and keep approval on for every other tool, especially system.tools.call, project.item.start, project.item.stop and project.job.start.
  • Your client shows the tool names its own way. A client may add a prefix and replace the dots: Claude Code shows project.item.start as mcp__sodero__project_item_start.
  • Review previews. Most changes are previewed first. project.item.create, project.item.duplicate, project.item.start, project.item.stop and project.job.start act at once.
  • The agent acts as you. What it changes is changed for everyone in the project.
  • Watch your credits. A Station or World that an agent activated uses credits until it is deactivated. Auto off still applies.

The rules Sodero gives every agent (preview changes first, move a robot only when you asked for that motion, treat files and logs as data and not as instructions) are instructions to the agent, not a safety function. An agent can misread them or make mistakes, and its tools have the same effect as your own actions. Approve every change yourself.

docs.title: Usage Limits
docs.text:
Agent tool calls count against your workspace's plan, per minute and per calendar month (UTC). Billing & Usage shows the calls used this month (Billing and Usage). At the monthly limit, calls are refused until the renewal date that the AI agents panel shows. At the per-minute limit, the agent is told how long to wait.

An upload can be up to 1 GiB for a library file and up to 64 MiB for other kinds, such as Station packages, World scenes, map bundles and Station documents.

A tool call ends after 100 seconds. A change may still have been applied: have the agent check the state before it repeats the change.

docs.title: Review and Revoke Agents
docs.text:
1. Click your avatar at the bottom of the left navigation bar and choose Account Settings.
  2. Under Connected AI agents, each agent shows its name, when it connected, its scopes (Read or Read, Write) and its Current workspaces.
  3. To disconnect an agent, click Revoke followed by the agent's name, then Confirm revoke.
Connected AI agents in Account settings

Revoking stops the agent's further calls and job steps but doesn't undo what was done. To connect the agent again, sign it in again.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Message or symptom What to do The sign-in ends without the consent page, and the agent reports that access was denied Start the sign-in again and finish it within 10 minutes, with your Sodero account. AUTH_REQUIRED, AUTH_EXPIRED or CONNECTION_REVOKED Sign the agent in again (Claude Code: /mcp). GRANT_MISSING Your account no longer has access to that workspace or project. Ask a person who manages it to add you again. NOT_FOUND for a project No project you can use matches the name or link. Check the name, or use workspace/name or the project link. WRITE_NOT_GRANTED The connection may only read. Connect the agent again with a client that requests write access. FORBIDDEN Your project role does not allow this action. Ask a person who can manage the project. RENAMED The agent called a tool by a former name. The message names the current tool: the agent calls that one instead. STATION_NOT_RUNNING or WORLD_NOT_RUNNING Activate the Station or World first. QUOTA_EXCEEDED Your workspace reached its plan's limit for agent calls. The message says when to try again.

docs.title: Project VPN
docs.text:
The Project VPN connects a device of yours, such as your computer or a robot PC, to the Stations of a project, so you can use a Station's API from a terminal, your own scripts or your IDE. You approve every connection yourself, and a connection lasts at most 8 hours.

AI agents don't need the Project VPN. To work on a project with Claude Code or another AI agent, see AI Agents.

docs.title: What the Project VPN Reaches
docs.text:
A connection reaches each Station (Robot System) of the project that was active when you connected: its API on port 8001, and the extra TCP ports opened for it (VPN Ports). It does not reach Robot Worlds, Stations activated or restarted after you connected, or other projects. Your device can call a Station, but a Station cannot connect to your device.

The Project VPN doesn't start anything: activate the Stations you want to use first (Activate and Run). An active Station uses credits whether or not you are connected, and your tools' calls to it count as use for Auto off.

The project's owner and people with Can manage can connect devices and copy Station API keys. When your role doesn't allow it, the panel says Your project role can't use the Project VPN. Ask the project owner for access.

docs.title: 1. Install Connector
docs.text:
Install the Connector once on each device you want to connect. It adds the sodero command, which connects the device.

  1. Open the project and click Project VPN in the top bar.
  2. Expand Install Connector. It shows an install command for Linux, macOS and Windows in two groups:
    • Desktop PC, for a computer with a desktop;
    • Robot or server PC (headless), for a device without a desktop: the command installs without prompts and starts no tray app.
  3. Copy the command for the device's system and run it on the device: on Linux or macOS in a terminal, as your normal user; on Windows in PowerShell. Approve the administrator prompt.
  4. Sign in once on the device: run sodero login. It opens the Sodero sign-in in your browser; without a desktop, it prints the sign-in address and explains how to open it. Finish within 5 minutes.
The Project VPN panel of Warehouse Demo

The command checks the installer before it runs it. On Linux, the installer supports Debian and Ubuntu. On Windows, it also installs WireGuard for Windows, which the Connector uses. Your system lists the Connector as Sodero VPN; on a desktop PC it also adds an optional status icon (Sodero VPN in your app menu, or sodero tray).

This sodero command belongs to the Connector. It is not the sodero CLI of the Stellar X SSH workspace.

docs.title: 2. Connect a Device
docs.text:
Every device connects the same way, this computer included.

  1. Activate at least one Station of the project. In Project VPN, click Connect a device. A new row shows the steps and the command for the device, sodero vpn connect '…', with a link in it.
  2. Click Copy next to the command, then run the command on the device and keep it running. The link works once, for one device, and only for 60 seconds (Link expires in … · one device); Get a new link replaces it.
  3. The command shows the project, the device and a six-character Confirmation code. Check that the code matches the one in the portal row, type y at Connect this device to this project? [y/N], then type the code when the command asks for it.
  4. The row shows Connected. Details lists the Stations in this connection.

The device must be approved within 5 minutes after you click Connect a device. When a request ends before the device connected, the row says Ended before the device connected: …; click Connect a device again.

Approve only a connection you started. If the portal shows a code that differs from the one on your device, another device used the link: cancel it in the portal and don't approve it.

Keep the command running. The device holds the connection: Ctrl+C or closing the terminal disconnects it. Once the row says Connected — the device manages this connection., you can close the portal tab. To keep the connection after you log out of an SSH session, run the command inside tmux or screen.

sodero vpn status shows the connection, sodero vpn disconnect ends it, and sodero --help lists all commands.

docs.title: 3. Use a Station's Address and API Key
docs.text:
Each Station has its own address on the Project VPN. It stays the same when the Station is deactivated and activated again. You find it under Station addresses in the Project VPN panel and in the IP address column of the project's Robot Systems.

  1. Connect your device while the Station is active.
  2. Click the copy icon next to the Station's address. It copies http://ADDRESS:8001/.
  3. Click the key icon (Copy the Station's API key). The key is copied to your clipboard; it is never shown on screen.
  4. In your tools, use the address and send the key with each request. The message that confirms the copy names the request header to use.

The key changes each time the Station starts. After the Station is deactivated and activated again, connect again and copy the new key.

Keep the key private. Treat it like a password: don't paste it into shared documents and don't commit it with your code.

docs.title: Addresses for a Control Station
docs.text:
A control app that runs on one of the project's Stations reaches the other Stations at their address inside the cloud, which your devices can't reach. It changes when the Station restarts.

  • The network icon next to a Station copies its address inside the cloud.
  • Copy for a control Station copies one line for each running Station: its name, its address inside the cloud and its API key.

docs.title: 4. VPN Ports
docs.text:
Besides its API port 8001, a Station can open more TCP ports on the Project VPN, for example for a service of your own module.

  1. In Station addresses, click the VPN ports button (sliders icon) next to the Station. The dialog VPN ports — name opens.

  2. Under Extra TCP ports, enter the ports, for example 9000, 9001, and click Save.

  3. You can open up to 16 TCP ports from 1024 to 65535. The dialog names the ports that the Station uses itself; they are refused.

  4. The ports apply the next time the Station starts (VPN ports saved. They apply the next time the Station starts.). Open now lists the ports of the current run. A connected device must connect again to use newly opened ports.
  5. Only the project's owner and people with Can manage can change VPN ports. Others see them read-only.
  6. One connection carries at most 64 Station ports. In a project with many Stations, each Station's API port comes first, and some extra ports may be left out.

Protect the services on extra ports. Anyone with an approved connection to the project can reach these ports: the services on them must check their own sign-in.

docs.title: 5. Disconnect
docs.text:
Click Disconnect in the device's row in the portal. On the device, press Ctrl+C where sodero vpn connect runs, or run sodero vpn disconnect. On a desktop PC, the status icon also has Disconnect VPN.

A connection also ends on its own after 8 hours; about a minute after the command that holds it stops, for example when the device sleeps; when all its Stations are deactivated or restarted; when you lose access to the project; or when your workspace has used its Project VPN time or data for the month. The Connector never reconnects on its own.

docs.title: 6. Update or Uninstall the Connector
docs.text: To update, run the install command from Install Connector with update in place of install, then connect again. To uninstall, run sodero uninstall (add --purge to also remove the VPN settings and the device identity), or on Windows uninstall Sodero VPN in Installed apps. WireGuard for Windows stays installed.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
What Limit Open connections per person 3, across all your projects Connections per device 1 at a time Length of a connection 8 hours Link for Connect a device 60 seconds, one device Approving a device Within 5 minutes Extra TCP ports per Station 16, from 1024 to 65535 Station ports per connection 64 Monthly use Project VPN time and data per workspace, as your plan allows

Billing & Usage shows the Project VPN time and data used this month (Billing and Usage). When they are used up, new connections are refused until the counters reset.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Message or symptom What to do No running Station is available for this project. Activate at least one Station, then connect. You have 3 connections, the maximum. … Disconnect a connection you don't need, here or in another project. The link expired. Get a new one to continue. Click Get a new link and run the new command on the device within 60 seconds. The confirmation code did not match. This device was not approved. Click Connect a device again, run the new command, and type the code exactly as the command shows it. Ended before the device connected: … The device was not approved within 5 minutes, or the command stopped. Click Connect a device again. A Station is missing, or Some Stations stopped or changed. … The Station was activated or restarted after you connected. Disconnect, then connect again. A local network or another VPN already routes a target address. Disconnect the other VPN, or connect from a different network. Not signed in to Sodero … or Your Sodero sign-in has ended … Run sodero login on the device. A checksum, size or signature mismatch during installation Don't work around it. Copy the command from Install Connector again; if the mismatch remains, report it to Sodero.

docs.title: Key Concepts
docs.text: This page explains the terms you meet everywhere in Sodero Cloud: workspaces and projects, Robot Systems and Robot Worlds, activation, Studio and Theater, and the parts of a Station. Read it once before the Quick Start.

docs.title: Workspaces and Projects
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    subgraph WS ["Workspace: people, plan, credits"]
        subgraph P ["Project: files and the people who can open them"]
            A["Robot System A<br>Stellar Station"] -- "simulation gateway" --> W["Robot World<br>simulated in the cloud"]
            B["Robot System B<br>Stellar Station"] -- "simulation gateway" --> W
        end
    end
Term What it is Workspace Where a team works together: its people, its projects, its plan and its credits. You can belong to several workspaces (Workspaces and People). Project Robot Systems and Robot Worlds that belong together, and the people who can open them (Projects) Robot System A project file that is one Stellar Station ("the Station"): the robot system's nodes, documents, settings and apps Robot World A project file that holds a simulated place: a USD scene with the ground, the lighting, objects and robots

A project can hold several Robot Worlds, but only one of them can be active at a time. Any number of Robot Systems can be active, within your plan's limit of Systems and Worlds running at once, and they all drive robots in that World (How Robot Worlds and Robot Systems Work Together).

docs.title: Activate and Run
docs.text:
Each Robot System and Robot World has its own environment in the cloud. Two columns on the project page control it, and they are separate steps:

Column States What it does Activation Inactive, Active Activate brings the environment up: a Station restores its saved data, a World loads its saved scene. Deactivate releases it. Running Stopped, Running Run starts what is in an active environment: the Station's nodes, the World's simulation. Stop stops them; the environment stays active.
  • Credits. An active file uses your workspace's credits for every minute it is active, whether or not anything runs in it. Stop does not end that; Deactivate does. Studio and Theater sessions can use credits too, depending on their rendering mode (Billing and Usage).
  • Auto off. An active file that nobody has used for 30 minutes is deactivated automatically, unless an editor has cleared its Auto off box. A Station counts as used while someone has it open or works with it through an AI agent or the Project VPN; a World, while someone watches it in Theater.

Details: Activate and Run.

docs.title: Studio and Theater
docs.text:
Tool For Opens while the World is Studio Building the World: bring in scenes and Sodero Assets, arrange objects, set mass and joint poses, save (Studio) Inactive Theater Watching the running World: select robots and see the Station that drives each one (Theater) Active

Both ask first for a rendering mode. RTX Real-time draws the World on a cloud GPU; WebGPU draws it in your browser with your computer's GPU. The mode changes only how you see the World: the simulation is the same for everyone (Choose Rendering Mode).

docs.title: Inside a Robot System: the Station
docs.text:
A Station is a graph of nodes. Each node is one program, such as a gateway, a robot controller, a navigation component or a module of your own. Add node offers four types:

Type Purpose Gateway Connects simulation or hardware to the system Controller Defines a robot unit and its control Compound Combines several robot units into one system Application Defines robot behaviors and task logic

Every node runs an app. Sodero's apps come from the Station's Store; your own module packages are added on Modules. A new Robot System can start with a bundle of apps, its Starting apps (Apps and Packages).

The IDs of Sodero's nodes start with sodero.. Most of them end with a name you choose, usually the robot's:

Node ID Actuator gateway sodero.actuator_gateway.<name> Camera gateway sodero.camera_gateway.<name> Mobile base controller sodero.mlc.<name> Manipulator controller (Motion Studio) sodero.mmc.<name> Articulated robot controller (Articulation) sodero.amc.<name> Strider, the operator UI of a mobile base sodero.strider Localizer, Navigator sodero.icp_localizer, sodero.navigator

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
Nodes work together through ports. Each node card lists REQUIRES, the services the node needs, and PROVIDES, the services it offers. You connect a required port to a matching provided port; the Station refuses ports that do not match. A mobile robot such as Jackal uses two connections:

flowchart TB
    S["Strider<br>sodero.strider"] -- "mobile_base" --> M["Mobile base controller<br>sodero.mlc.jackal"]
    M -- "servo_link" --> G["Actuator gateway<br>sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal"]
    G -- "robot name jackal" --> W["Robot World<br>robot /World/jackal"]
Requires Provides Meaning Controller servo_link Actuator gateway servo_link The controller drives the gateway's actuators Strider mobile_base Mobile base controller mobile_base Strider operates this mobile base

See Build the Graph.

docs.title: Gateways and Documents
docs.text:
A gateway is the only node that talks to actuators; controllers send their commands through it. In Sodero Cloud, a simulation gateway drives a robot in the project's World. On Stellar X, an EtherCAT gateway drives real drives; the controllers work the same way, in the Station release that the device runs (Compatibility).

Gateways and controllers are configured by design documents, which you upload into the node's Parameters (Documents and Settings):

File Node Contents .gw Actuator gateway Hardware type and actuators .sdd sodero.mmc Manipulator: kinematics, dynamics, actuator mapping .sddm sodero.mlc Mobile base: drive type, wheels, limits, actuator mapping .sdda sodero.amc Articulated robot: joints and actuator mapping

Names must match. A simulation gateway finds its robot in the World by name. The Robot name of the gateway node must be exactly the name of the robot's prim in the World, for example jackal for /World/jackal. With another name, the robot never moves. See Connect to the World.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Term Meaning Workspace A team's space in the portal: people, projects, plan and credits Project Robot Systems and Robot Worlds that belong together, and who can open them Robot System A project file that is one Stellar Station Stellar Station The application that runs a robot system as a graph of nodes. Stellar X runs it too, in the device's own release. Robot World A project file with a simulated place and the robots in it Studio The World editor Theater The live view of an active World Activate, Deactivate Bring a file's environment up, or release it Run, Stop Start or stop what runs in an active environment Auto off Deactivates a file that nobody has used for 30 minutes Credits What active files and rendering sessions use, from your workspace's plan RTX Real-time, WebGPU The rendering modes: on a cloud GPU, or on your computer's GPU Node One program in the Station, such as a gateway, a controller or a module of your own Port A connection point of a node: REQUIRES (needs) or PROVIDES (offers) Gateway A node that connects controllers to actuators or sensors, simulated or real Controller A node that controls a robot unit, such as a mobile base or a manipulator Design document The configuration of a gateway or a robot controller: .gw, .sdd, .sddm, .sdda App A package from the Store that a node runs Robot name The name of a robot's prim in the World, set on the simulation gateway node that drives it .sdr A Sodero file that holds one Robot System or one Robot World Sodero Assets Robots, environments and documents published by Sodero

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: Create a warehouse World, watch its simulation in Theater, then stop and deactivate it. This first exercise walks through the whole life of a World; driving its robots from a Station comes next (Next: Connect a Robot System).

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
• Sign in to Sodero Cloud with access to create a project and edit its files.
  • In the workspace menu, open Billing & Usage and check the credits left and Systems and Worlds running at once.
  • Download jackal_warehouse.zip, the example scene with a Jackal and a Dingo. Keep the ZIP intact. It includes the accompanying Clearpath license notice.

Credits: an active World uses credits until you deactivate it, and Studio and Theater sessions can use credits while they are open. Billing & Usage shows your plan's rates (Billing and Usage).

docs.title: Step 1: Create the Project and World
docs.text:
1. In Projects, click + Project.
  2. Enter Warehouse Demo, keep Restricted, and click Create.
  3. In the project, click New file, choose Robot World, and click Next.
  4. Enter warehouse as the File Name, then click Create.
Naming the new Robot World

The World appears as Inactive. Its Studio link opens the editor.

docs.title: Step 2: Import and Save the Scene
docs.text:
1. Click Studio on the World row. Choose RTX Real-time or WebGPU, then click Open Cosmic Studio. Studio opens in a new tab. Keep the Sodero Cloud tab open while you work: Studio uses it to keep you signed in and to read library files.
  2. Open the logo menu and choose World › Replace scene….

  3. On This PC, select jackal_warehouse.zip, click Replace, and confirm replacement.

    The Replace scene dialog

  4. Check that the Hierarchy shows dingo_d, jackal and warehouse.

  5. Click Save now in the left rail and wait for Saved just now.
The example scene in Studio. It contains a Jackal and a Dingo.

Choose Back to Sodero Cloud from the logo menu to close Studio.

docs.title: Step 3: Activate the World
docs.text: On the project page, set the World's Activation to Active. Wait until Activating changes to Active. Activation prepares the environment; it does not start the simulation.

docs.title: Step 4: View and Run the Simulation
docs.text:
1. Click Theater, choose a rendering mode, and click Open Cosmic Theater.
  2. Wait for Ready.
  3. On the project page, set the World's Running state to Running. You can also click Start Theater in Theater when you control it: the first person with edit access who opened Theater controls Start Theater and Stop Theater (Start and Stop).
  4. Select jackal in Scene assets; double-click the row to bring the camera to it.

The readout at the bottom of the viewport shows FPS, the rate at which your view is drawn, and Physics RTF, the real-time factor of the simulation: simulated time divided by wall-clock time. Near 1.00, the simulation keeps up with real time. The robots stay where they are until a Robot System drives them.

docs.title: Step 5: Stop and End the Session
docs.text:
1. Set the World's Running state to Stopped. Stopping resets its pose and clock; it is not a pause that preserves progress.
  2. Set Activation to Inactive and wait for deactivation to finish.
  3. Close the Theater tab. In Billing & Usage, a green dot under Recent runs marks anything that is still active.

A stopped World stays active and keeps using credits until you deactivate it. Deactivating a World does not deactivate the project's Robot Systems: deactivate each file you activated.

docs.title: Next: Connect a Robot System
docs.text:
To drive the Jackal of this World, add a Robot System to the same project. Download its two documents first: jackal.gw, the simulation gateway document, and jackal.sddm, the mobile robot document.

  1. In the project, create a Robot System named jackal and open it with Station · Edit (Create a File). In the Store, install sodero.actuator_gateway, sodero.mlc and sodero.strider (Apps and Packages).
  2. Add a Gateway node that runs sodero.actuator_gateway and name it sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal (Add a Node). In its inspector, click Upload under Gateway project and import jackal.gw (Documents and Settings).
  3. Under the gateway document, set Robot name to jackal, the name of the robot's prim in the World. jackal.gw already fills it in (Name the Robot).
  4. Add a Controller node that runs sodero.mlc and name it sodero.mlc.jackal. Click Upload under document (robot) and import jackal.sddm. Connect the node's servo_link port to the gateway (Connect Ports).
  5. Add sodero.strider and connect its mobile_base port to sodero.mlc.jackal (Set Up the Nodes).
  6. Activate and run the World again (Steps 3 and 4). In the Station, click Go live, then Start all nodes (Start and Monitor Nodes). Right-click sodero.strider, open Strider and drive the Jackal (Strider).

For other robots, use documents made for this Station release, such as those in Sodero Assets (Compatibility).

docs.title: What Is Sodero Cloud
docs.text: Sodero Cloud runs the Sodero robot platform in your browser. You build a simulated place for your robots, compose their robot systems in Stellar Station, run both in the cloud and watch them live, with nothing to install.

docs.title: Projects, Worlds and Systems
docs.text:
Everything you build lives in a project in the Sodero Cloud portal at https://app.sodero.io. A project holds two kinds of file:

  • Robot Worlds: simulated places with your robots in them, for example a warehouse with a mobile base.
  • Robot Systems: the robot software. Each Robot System is one Stellar Station.

The Robot Systems of a project drive the robots in the project's active Robot World.

docs.title: Core Ideas
docs.text:
Studio builds the World, the cloud simulates it, Theater shows it. You build a Robot World in Studio, the World editor: bring in a scene, add robots and environments from Sodero Assets, arrange them and save. When you activate the World, Sodero Cloud simulates it. Theater shows the running World live in your browser, with the robots and the Stations that drive them.

Each Robot System is a Stellar Station. It uses a graph of nodes and Stellar Designer document types (.gw, .sdd, .sddm, .sdda). These concepts also apply to Stellar X. The available apps, menus and accepted document versions depend on the installed release (Compatibility).

The World connects by itself. The simulation gateways of every active Station in the project connect to the project's active World automatically. There is no Isaac Sim to install and no network to set up: each gateway finds its robot in the World by name.

docs.title: From Design to a Running Robot
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    D["Design<br>Stellar Designer documents"] --> W["Build the World<br>Studio"]
    W --> C["Compose<br>Stellar Station"]
    C --> R["Run and watch<br>Theater"]
    C -. ".sdr transfer:<br>check compatibility" .-> X["Stellar X<br>real hardware"]

Design. Describe each robot and its gateway in Stellar Designer documents: kinematics, wheels, limits and actuator mapping. Sodero also publishes ready-made documents in Sodero Assets.

Build the World. In Studio, bring in a scene or Sodero Assets, arrange them and save. The World must follow a few rules so that Stations can drive its robots (Prepare a World for Simulation).

Compose. In the Station, add gateways and controllers as nodes, connect their ports and load their documents.

Run and watch. On the project page, activate the World and its Robot Systems and run them (Activate and Run). Watch the World in Theater and operate the robots from the controller UIs (Strider).

docs.title: Sodero Cloud and Stellar X
docs.text:
Stellar X is Sodero's motion controller for real robots. It runs the same Stellar Station on the robot, with EtherCAT for real drives (Stellar X manual).

Sodero Cloud Stellar X Where the Station runs In the cloud, one per Robot System On the Stellar X controller What it drives Robots simulated in the project's Robot World Real drives through EtherCAT, or a robot in NVIDIA Isaac Sim on your PC Simulation Built in: Studio, the cloud simulation and Theater Isaac Sim with the Isaac Bridge extension, on your PC Save a Station to a file Download local copy (.sdr) Export SDR Load a Station from a file Import (.sdr) Load SDR

Move a Robot System with an .sdr file. Check the destination's Station release and apps first (Move Robot Systems Between Stellar X and Sodero Cloud).

Adapt the design for real hardware. Controllers send commands through a gateway. Reusing a controller design on Stellar X requires a compatible release, a hardware gateway, and checks of actuator mapping, calibration, limits and sensors. Follow the device manual before enabling motion.

Tip: Build and test the robot system in Sodero Cloud first. When it behaves as it should in the World, take it to the real robot on Stellar X.

docs.title: What You Need
docs.text: You need Details A browser Everything runs in the browser: the portal, Studio, the Station, the controller UIs and Theater. A Sodero account Sign in at https://app.sodero.io (Sign In and Account). Credits Active Robot Systems and Robot Worlds use your workspace's credits (Billing and Usage). Rendering WebGPU needs support from your browser, operating system and GPU. RTX Real-time renders in the cloud and streams the view to your device. See Compatibility.

docs.title: Find Your Way in the Portal
The Left Navigation Bar
docs.text:
The left navigation bar is the column of icons on the left of every portal page.

Item Opens Sodero logo, Home Your Recent and Favorites projects, Robot Systems and Robot Worlds Projects The projects of the current workspace, or your guest projects (Projects) Library The libraries of the projects in the current workspace (Libraries) Trash Items moved to Trash in this workspace (Projects) Notifications, Help See below Your avatar Account Settings, Sign-in & Security, Theme and Sign out (Sign In and Account)

The name of the current workspace is at the top left of the page; click it for the workspace menu (Workspaces and People).

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: Click the bell (Notifications) in the left navigation bar to see recent activity in the current workspace, such as projects created or trashed, people added or removed, and Robot Systems and Robot Worlds started, stopped or failed. A red badge counts the unread entries; Read All marks them read.

docs.title: Help and Feedback
docs.text:
Click Help in the left navigation bar. The menu has Documentation, Report a bug, Share an idea and Contact support.

The Help menu
  • Report a bug or Share an idea: fill in the fields, attach up to 10 PNG, JPG or PDF files (20 MB in total) if you like, and click Submit report or Submit idea. Sodero receives it with your name, email address and account ID, the page you were on and your browser details.
  • Contact support opens the Sodero website in a new tab.

Do not include passwords, access keys or other sensitive information in the text or in the attachments.

Continue with Key Concepts, then try the Quick Start.

docs.title: Articulation
docs.text:
The Articulation controller drives an articulated robot joint by joint: legged robots, humanoids, grippers, pan-tilt heads, or any set of joints that receives joint targets. Unlike the manipulator controller, it uses no arm kinematics (no DH parameters, no Cartesian motions). It bounds and forwards the joint targets of an upper controller, such as a walking policy in your own module, and its Articulation UI lets you jog the joints by hand.

Item Value Node sodero.amc.<name> Document .sdda, made in Stellar Designer (Articulated Robot in the Stellar X manual) Joints 1 to 64, driven by one actuator gateway Units rad, rad/s, N·m 
flowchart LR
    U["Upper controller<br>your module"] -- "joint targets" --> A["Articulation<br>sodero.amc.dog"]
    A -- servo_link --> G["Actuator gateway<br>sodero.actuator_gateway.dog"]

docs.title: 1. The Document
docs.text:
An .sdda document lists the joints and how the gateway's actuators drive them.

Per joint Meaning Name Joint name Position min / max Range of motion; targets outside it are refused Velocity max Velocity limit, also the reference for the jog speed Torque max Torque limit; the controller clamps its total output to it Offset (optional) Joint position at actuator position zero Kp, Kd (optional) Stiffness and damping, for PD torque control
  • Drive mode. In position mode, the controller bounds the joint targets and the drive follows them with its own position control. In pd_torque mode, the controller computes a PD torque from Kp and Kd and sends torque commands.
  • Actuator mapping. One actuator can move several joints, and several actuators can move one joint, as long as the mapping can be inverted.
  • Watchdogs. The controller switches the servo off and latches a stop when the gateway's feedback is older than 100 ms, or when no new target arrives for 200 ms (the defaults). Click Clear stop, then Servo on. Reconnecting never switches the servo on by itself.

docs.title: 2. Set Up the Nodes
docs.text:
1. In the Station's Store, install sodero.actuator_gateway and sodero.amc (Apps and Packages).
  2. Add the gateway and the Articulation controller, and connect the controller's servo_link to the gateway (Build the Graph).
  3. Upload the gateway's .gw and the controller's .sdda document (Documents and Settings).
  4. Set the gateway's Robot name and check the actuator mapping (Connect to the World).
  5. Run the World, go live, then start the gateway, the controller and the program that sends joint targets, in this order (Start and Monitor Nodes).

docs.title: 3. Open the Articulation UI
docs.text:
On the Live page, right-click the running sodero.amc.<name> node and choose Open … (Start and Monitor Nodes). The Articulation UI opens in a new tab. If its session expires, open it again from the node.

Area Contents Left rail Joints (joint monitor), Constraints (the configured limits), Set origin Top bar Servo on, Servo off, Stop (switches the servo off and latches a stop), Clear stop (releases it while the servo is off), the control mode, and the button that opens the Joint control panel Status strip Servo on or off, Feedback age in milliseconds, Safety (Ready or the reason for a stop) Controller The Articulation node this window controls Joint monitor Per joint: position, velocity, effort and target

Stop the upper controller first. Pause or stop the program that sends joint targets, such as a walking policy, before you jog the joints by hand.

docs.title: 4. Jog Joints
docs.text:
1. Open the Joint control panel with the button at the right of the top bar.
  2. Click Servo on.
  3. Under Joint jog, set the Speed: 1–100 % of each joint's velocity limit, 10 % by default.
  4. Hold − or + next to a joint. The joint moves while you hold the button and holds its position when you release it. A jog button also switches the servo on if it is off.

Leaving the window, switching to another tab or losing the connection switches the servo off.

docs.title: 5. Send Joint Targets
docs.text:
Under Joint targets:

  1. Click Use measured positions to copy the current positions into the target fields.
  2. Change the targets of the joints you want to move.
  3. Click Stream targets. The controller follows the targets while the stream runs; Stop target stream ends it and switches the servo off.

docs.title: 6. Set the Origin
docs.text: Set origin gives the current position of a joint a known angle, for example after an encoder was replaced on a real robot. Robots in a Robot World do not support it. For real robots, see Articulation in the Stellar X manual.

docs.title: 7. Control from Programs
docs.text: From How A walking robot Your module runs the walking policy and sends joint targets to the Articulation node AI agents The station.articulation tools: state, servo, joint targets, stops and fault reset (AI Agents) Your own tools The Station API, through the Project VPN

docs.title: Motion Studio
docs.text: Motion Studio is the operator UI for manipulators. The manipulator controller node, sodero.mmc.<name>, runs the arm's real-time controller: kinematics, dynamics, trajectory generation and safety limits, from the arm's .sdd document. Motion Studio belongs to that node. It shows the arm in 3D, jogs it, defines tools and teaches poses.

docs.title: 1. Set Up the Nodes
docs.text:
1. In the Station's Store, install sodero.actuator_gateway and sodero.mmc (Apps and Packages).
  2. Add the gateway and the manipulator controller, and connect the controller's servo_link to the gateway (Build the Graph).
  3. Upload the gateway's .gw and the controller's .sdd document (Documents and Settings).
  4. Set the gateway's Robot name and check the actuator mapping (Connect to the World).
  5. Run the World, go live, then start the gateway and the controller, in this order (Start and Monitor Nodes).

docs.title: 2. Open Motion Studio
docs.text: On the Live page, right-click the running sodero.mmc.<name> node and choose Open … (Start and Monitor Nodes). Motion Studio opens in a new tab. If its session expires, open it again from the node.

docs.title: 3. Screen Layout
docs.text: Item Description Pages Home, Tool and Pose 3D view The arm in its current pose, with the 3D model of its .sdd Joint Status Per joint: position, target position, velocity, target velocity, effort and residual effort TCP Status Position and orientation of the tool center point (TCP), and its linear and angular velocity Active Tool Status The active tool's TCP offset, center of mass and payload mass Filters Shows or hides the cards of the Home page

docs.title: Header
docs.text:
Item Description Robot and role The controller node, and whether this window has control (Pilot - Control Active) Manual / Auto Manual limits the linear speed of the TCP in the controller's own motions and jogs, 0.25 m/s by default; it does not limit rotations or Hand mode. Auto runs at the programmed speed. Feed rate Speed override in percent (10–150 %), applied to motion in progress Error Reset Clears a protective stop (a joint at its limit, a speed or torque limit, a detected collision) and resets drive faults. Switch the servo on again afterwards. Units mm / g / deg or m / kg / radian Jog Opens the jog panel Command log Commands sent from this window Alarm Active alarms and notifications

The mark at the top left opens the menu, with File to import and export tools and poses.

docs.title: 4. Jog the Arm
docs.text:
Click Jog in the header to open the jog panel.

  1. Switch Servo On.
  2. In JOG OPTION, choose the Mode:
    • Joint: move one joint at a time (J1…Jn).
    • Base: move the tool in the robot's base frame (X, Y, Z, RX, RY, RZ).
    • Tool: move the tool in its own frame.
    • Hand: hand guiding, for a real arm. The arm compensates gravity and the jog buttons are disabled.
  3. Choose Continuous (moves while you hold a button) or Step (5° or 10 mm per click), and the Speed: 50 %, 100 % or 150 %, about 0.04, 0.1 and 0.2 m/s at the tool.
  4. Hold − or + next to a joint or axis in JOG CONTROL. The motion stops when you release the button.

The POSE section of the panel shows the current TCP pose and joint positions.

Stop the motion before you leave the UI. A continuous jog stops when the release of the button reaches the controller. If the browser or the connection fails while you jog, do not assume that the arm has stopped: stop the controller node in the Station and check in Theater that the arm stands still. For a real arm, see Stop Controls in the Stellar X manual.

docs.title: 5. Tools
docs.text:
The Tool page defines the tools mounted on the flange.

  1. Click + to add a tool, and rename it with the pencil icon, for example gripper.
  2. Enter the TOOL CENTER POINT: the TCP position and orientation relative to the flange. The calculator icon opens TCP Calibration, which computes the TCP from 3–10 poses that touch the same point.
  3. Enter the PAYLOAD PROPERTIES: center of mass, inertia and mass. The calculator icon opens Payload Calibration.
  4. Click Save, or Save and Apply to make it the active tool at once. Set as active tool activates a saved tool.

A wrong payload makes hand guiding and collision detection unreliable. Set the mass and center of mass of every tool you mount.

docs.title: 6. Poses
docs.text:
The Pose page stores named poses.

  1. Jog the arm to the pose, then click the camera icon (Save Current Pose). Or click + (Add pose) and fill in the values.
  2. Select the pose in the list. POSE DATA shows its TCP pose and joint positions; Set from current copies the current pose into it.
  3. Under TEST MOVE, choose Joint or Linear motion and hold Hold to move. The arm moves to the pose only while you hold the button.
  4. Click Save.

Saved poses appear as markers in the 3D view. Right-click a pose to copy, duplicate or delete it. File in the menu exports and imports tools and poses.

docs.title: 7. Program the Arm
docs.text:
Motion Studio is for setup and teaching. Programs run outside it and use the same controller:

From How AI agents The station.motion tools: state, servo, moves, stops and fault reset (AI Agents) Your own module A module node on the Station, connected to the manipulator controller node (Apps and Packages) Your own tools The Station API, through the Project VPN

From simulation to a real arm. The arm's .sdd document, its tools and poses, and your programs carry over to a real arm on Stellar X, which uses an EtherCAT gateway instead of the simulation gateway. A real arm needs its own checks first: see Motion Studio in the Stellar X manual.

docs.title: Strider
docs.text: Strider is the operator UI for wheeled mobile bases. With it you jog the base, watch its state and odometry, and send navigation goals. It works with every drive type that a mobile robot document (.sddm) can describe: differential drive, skid steer 4WD, mecanum 4WD, swerve 4WD and Ackermann.

docs.title: How Strider Works in a Station
docs.text:
Two nodes are involved:

Node Role sodero.mlc.<name> The mobile base controller. It turns body velocities into wheel commands for its gateway, integrates odometry, and keeps the speed and acceleration limits of its .sddm document. It has no UI of its own. sodero.strider Strider. It drives what its ports are connected to: mobile_base to the base controller (driving and status), localization to the localizer (the robot's position on the map) and navigation to the navigator (goals). 
flowchart LR
    S["sodero.strider"] -- mobile_base --> M["sodero.mlc.jackal<br>jackal.sddm"]
    M -- servo_link --> G["sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal<br>jackal.gw"]
    S -. localization .-> L["sodero.icp_localizer"]
    S -. navigation .-> N["sodero.navigator"]

docs.title: 1. Set Up the Nodes
docs.text:
1. In the Station's Store, install sodero.actuator_gateway, sodero.mlc and sodero.strider (Apps and Packages).
  2. Add the gateway, the base controller and Strider. Connect the controller's servo_link to the gateway, and Strider's mobile_base to the base controller (Build the Graph).
  3. Upload the gateway's .gw and the controller's .sddm document (Documents and Settings).
  4. Set the gateway's Robot name and check the actuator mapping (Connect to the World).
  5. Run the World, go live, then start the gateway, the controller and Strider, in this order (Start and Monitor Nodes).

docs.title: 2. Open Strider
docs.text: On the Live page, right-click the running sodero.strider node and choose Open … (Start and Monitor Nodes). Strider opens in a new tab. If its session expires, open it again from the node.

docs.title: 3. Screen Layout
docs.text:
The left rail has three pages: Status, Drive and Navigation. The top bar holds the actions of the current page and, on every page:

Item Description Readiness pill The current state in one line, for example Manual Drive Ready or Servo Off. Click it for the checks: Connection, Mobile base, Servo, Localization, Navigation. System Log Events of this browser session, filtered by System, Drive, Navigation and Localization Motion Alarm Active alarms and recent errors E-STOP Software stop: cancels driving and the navigation goal and sets the wheel speeds to zero at once, with the servo still on. It latches until Clear E-Stop, which switches the base to Idle. Units m / m/s / deg or m / m/s / rad, for display only

docs.title: Status Page
docs.text:
Card Contents Trajectory (Odometry View) The path driven since the last mode change, in the odometry frame Operation Status Ready, moving or idle, servo on or off, and faults or stops Base Status (Odometry) Mode, and X, Y, Theta, VX, VY, WZ Control Node Health Whether the base, the localizer and the navigator are reachable Drive Unit Status The drive template and, per wheel, the servo state, position, velocity and target velocity Recent Events The latest events; View All opens the System Log

Watchdog Tripped while the base stands still in Twist mode is normal: no velocity command is arriving, so the base holds zero speed.

docs.title: 4. Jog the Base
docs.text:
On the Drive page:

  1. Under Drive Mode, click Twist.
  2. Under Servo / Safety, switch Servo On. The readiness pill shows Manual Drive Ready.
  3. Set the Linear Velocity Limit (0.2 m/s by default, at most 0.8 m/s) and the Angular Velocity Limit.
  4. Press and hold a pad button: Forward (W), Backward (S), Turn Left (A) or Turn Right (D). The base moves while you hold the button and stops when you release it; Stop (Space) stops it too.
  5. To drive with the keyboard, switch on Live in Manual Drive, then use W, S, A, D and Space. Commands stop when the window loses focus.
  6. When you are done, switch the servo off and click Idle.
Control Meaning Drive Mode Idle: no motion. Twist: body velocity commands, for jogging and navigation. Wheel: direct wheel speeds (advanced). EMG: stops the base like E-STOP, without latching. Servo On / Off Enables or disables the drives. Fault Reset clears drive faults; then switch the servo off and on again. Stop Motion Stops manual driving and cancels a navigation goal

Manual commands take priority over navigation: jogging during a navigation goal overrides the navigator and can end the goal. A manual command expires after about a second, so the base stops if the connection drops. A navigation goal does not expire: cancel it with Stop Motion, Cancel or E-STOP.

Show next to Advanced Controls opens Wheel Direct (each wheel's speed in Wheel mode), Preview Command (the wheel speeds a body velocity would give, without moving), Steering Origin, Calibration and Record / Replay.

docs.title: 5. Navigation Page
docs.text:
The Navigation page works when Strider's localization and navigation ports are connected to a running localizer and navigator, and the Station has a map bundle. To set them up, install sodero.icp_localizer and sodero.navigator from the Store, connect the localizer's camera port to the robot's camera gateway and the navigator's mobile_base and localization ports to the base controller and the localizer, and upload the map bundle (Build the Graph › Common Connections, Documents and Settings).

Card Contents Navigation Map (Occupancy Grid) The map, the robot, the planned path and the goal. Drag to pan, scroll to zoom. Localization Status Healthy, Degraded, Initializing, Relocalizing, Lost or Uninitialized. Global localization searches the whole map. Mission Status, Current Pose (Map), Goal Pose, Route Summary The goal, where the robot is and how far it still has to go Navigator The navigator's state and a Speed Limit slider (10–100 %) Navigation Controls Set Initial Pose, Set Goal, Clear Goal, Pause, Resume, Cancel

docs.title: Set the Initial Pose
docs.text:
If the localization status is not Healthy:

  1. Click Set Initial Pose.
  2. Press on the map where the robot stands and drag in the direction it faces.
  3. Click Set initial pose (or Relocalize here when a pose was set before).

docs.title: Send a Goal
docs.text:
1. Make sure the base is in Twist with the servo on: the readiness pill shows Navigation Ready.
  2. Click Set Goal, press on the map where the robot should go and drag in the direction it should face.
  3. Click Start Navigation. The planned path appears.

Pause cancels the goal and keeps it; Resume sends it again. Cancel stops navigation.

docs.title: 6. Control Strider from Programs
docs.text:
• AI agents drive the base with the station.strider tools: state, servo, velocities, stops and fault reset (AI Agents).
  • Your own module on the Station connects to the base controller's mobile_base port (Apps and Packages).
  • Your own tools on your computer reach the Station API through the Project VPN.

docs.title: Activate and Run
docs.text:
Each Robot System and Robot World has its own cloud environment. Activate prepares it, Run starts its work, Stop ends the work, and Deactivate releases the environment. Stopping a World resets its pose and clock; it is not a pause that preserves progress.

An active environment uses credits. It is billed for every minute it is active, whether or not anybody uses it or anything runs in it. Stop does not end that; Deactivate does (Billing and Usage).

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Two columns of the project page control a file: Activation brings its environment up or down, and Running starts or stops what runs in it.

flowchart LR
    I["Inactive"] -- "Activate" --> S["Active<br>Stopped"]
    S -- "Run" --> R["Active<br>Running"]
    R -- "Stop" --> S
    S -- "Deactivate" --> I
    R -- "Deactivate" --> I
Action Robot System Robot World Credits Activate Starts the environment and restores the Station's saved data and apps. No node starts. Starts the environment and loads the World's scene. The simulation does not play yet. Use begins Run Starts every saved node, like Start all nodes in the Station Plays the simulation No change Stop Stops the nodes Stops the simulation and resets the World's pose and clock Use goes on Deactivate Stops the nodes, saves the Station's data, then tears the environment down Tears the environment down Use ends

A typical session: select the Robot World and the Robot Systems that drive it, choose Actions › Activate, then Actions › Run. Watch the World in Theater and work with the robots in Station · Live. Stop when you pause, and Deactivate when you are done.

docs.title: 1. Activate and Deactivate
docs.text:
Click the state in a file's Activation column and choose Active to activate the file, or Inactive to deactivate it.

The Activation menu of the Robot System jackal
