While the file activates, it shows Activating and the current step, for example Station starting or World starting. It is usually Active after about a minute.

jackal activating: Station starting State Meaning Inactive Not active. Uses no credits. Activating Coming up. You can already choose Inactive. Active Up, and using credits Deactivating Going down. This cannot be interrupted. Error The activation failed, or the environment stopped unexpectedly. Open the menu for the reason.
  • After an Error, choose Active to try again, or select the file and choose Actions › Deactivate to release it.
  • Only one Robot World per project can be active (How Robot Worlds and Robot Systems Work Together).

A chip next to the column shows each result, for example Environment active or Failed. Click Failed to read the message.

While a request runs, the menu also offers Cancel workflow (no rollback). It stops the request but undoes nothing: an environment that already came up stays active, and keeps using credits, until you deactivate it.

docs.title: 2. Run and Stop
docs.text:
Once a file is Active, click the state in its Running column and choose Running or Stopped.

A World without a scene cannot run: build it in Studio first. Stopped keeps the file active, so it keeps using credits.

State Meaning Running Operations are running Partly running Robot System only: some nodes did not start. A Failed badge and a banner above the tables explain why. Open Station · Live and read that node's log (Start and Monitor Nodes). Stopped Operations are stopped. Also shown while the file is not active. Error The World reported an error - The state cannot be read. People with Can view always see -.

docs.title: 3. Open a File
docs.text:
The Actions column holds the links that open a file in a new browser tab. A dimmed link tells you on hover why it cannot open now.

Link Opens when Opens Station · Edit The Robot System is not active The Station editor. Its Go live button activates the Station. Station · Live The Robot System is Active The running Station (Stellar Station) Studio The Robot World is Inactive or in Error The World editor (Studio) Theater The Robot World is Active The live view of the World (Theater)

Opening a file never starts nodes or plays a World. To edit an active World in Studio, deactivate it first.

docs.title: Choose Rendering Mode
docs.text:
Before Studio or Theater opens, the portal asks how to draw the World on your screen.

Mode Draws the World RTX Real-time On a cloud GPU, with advanced materials and lighting. Each Studio or Theater tab in this mode runs its own cloud renderer, which uses credits. WebGPU In your browser, on this device's GPU, with no cloud GPU. Performance depends on your hardware. Your plan may still count WebGPU sessions (Billing and Usage).

Pick a mode and click Open Cosmic Studio or Open Cosmic Theater. Remember on this device. preselects your choice next time. The mode only changes how you see the World, not the simulation, and each person chooses their own.

docs.title: 4. Several Files at Once
docs.text:
Editors and managers can handle several files together from the selection bar.

  1. Select the files: click their rows, or tick the box at the end of a row. A selection holds any number of Robot Systems and at most one Robot World.
  2. Open Actions and choose an item.
  3. Follow the progress in the files' chips and in the log under the selection bar.
jackal and warehouse selected, with the Actions menu open

The menu offers Activate, Run, Stop and Deactivate, which act on every selected file as How It Works describes.

  • There is no single step that activates and runs: choose Run once the files are active.
  • The files are handled independently: if one fails, the others carry on.
  • Sodero carries on with a request after you close the page. Back on the project page, click the refresh button to follow it again.

docs.title: 5. Auto Off
docs.text:
Auto off deactivates an active file that nobody has used for 30 minutes (the default). It is on for every file unless an editor turns it off.

File In use while Robot System Someone has the Station open in a browser tab, or an AI agent or a Project VPN tool works with the Station Robot World Someone watches it in Theater

Running nodes and a playing World do not count as use: a World left playing with no viewer is deactivated like an idle one.

When nobody is using an active file, a yellow countdown appears under its state: Auto off in N min. It stops when somebody opens the file, and starts a minute or two after the last person leaves.

docs.title: Turn Auto Off Off
docs.text:
To keep a file active on purpose, clear its Auto off box. The portal warns that the file is billed for every minute it stays active: click Turn off and keep billing to confirm, or Keep it on.

The warning before Auto off is turned off

The file then stays active, and keeps using credits, until somebody deactivates it. Tick the box to turn Auto off on again.

Deactivate what you no longer need. Auto off is a safety net, not a replacement for deactivating.

docs.title: 6. Troubleshooting
docs.text: Message What to do Activating and deactivating needs edit access to this project. Your role is Can view. Ask a manager for Can edit. Another Robot World is already running in this project Deactivate the active World first. This workspace has run out of credits. … See When Credits Run Out. The … plan runs at most N Systems and Worlds at once. … Deactivate another Robot System or Robot World first; stopping it is not enough. Environment failed to activate Read the reason under it, then choose Active to try again.

docs.title: Robot Systems and Robot Worlds
docs.text:
A project holds two kinds of file: Robot Systems, which run robot software in Stellar Station, and Robot Worlds, which simulate the place where the robots work.

File What it is Edit it in Work with it live in Robot System One Stellar Station ("the Station"): its node graph, documents, settings and apps Station · Edit Station · Live Robot World A simulated environment: a scene with your robots, the ground and lighting Studio Theater

Design documents, such as gateway documents (.gw) and robot documents (.sdd, .sddm, .sdda), are not project files: they live inside a Station or in a library.

docs.title: 1. Create a File
docs.text:
1. In the project, click New file. An empty project also offers Create new file.
  2. Choose Robot System or Robot World and click Next.
  3. Enter a File Name (up to 20 characters) and, if you like, a Description (up to 40 characters).
  4. For a Robot System, choose its Starting apps.
  5. Click Create. The new file appears in its table, Inactive.

docs.title: Starting Apps
docs.text:
Starting apps offers bundles of Store apps for the new Station: Empty (No apps; install what you need from the Store.), Manipulator, Mobile robot and Legged. The apps install when the Station first starts. If some apps could not be added, the portal names them: install them from the Station's Store (Apps and Packages).

A new Robot World has no scene yet. Open it with Studio to build one (Studio); until then it has nothing to run.

docs.title: 2. Import an .sdr File
docs.text:
A Sodero file (.sdr) holds one Robot System or one Robot World. Importing it creates a new file in the project, with the name and description stored in the .sdr.

  1. In the project, click Import. An empty project also offers Import file.
  2. Choose the source: From your PC (drag the file onto the dialog, or click Choose file) or Project Library (the .sdr files in this project's library).
  3. Click Import.
Importing an .sdr file from your PC

The new file appears under Robot Systems or Robot Worlds, depending on what the .sdr holds.

docs.title: Move Robot Systems Between Stellar X and Sodero Cloud
docs.text:
A Robot System moves as an .sdr file between Sodero Cloud (Download local copy, Import) and a Stellar X controller (Export SDR, Load SDR):

  • From Stellar X: export the Station on the controller with Export SDR, then import the file into a project.
  • To Stellar X: download a local copy of the Robot System, then load it on the controller with Load SDR (Backup and Restore in the Stellar X manual).

Check the release and the apps. The destination must run a Station release that accepts the file's graph and documents (Compatibility). An .sdr does not contain installed packages: after importing one from Stellar X, install the apps its nodes need; before loading one on Stellar X, install the packages the Station uses on the controller. Keep the original file until the moved Robot System works.

A Robot World's .sdr opens in Sodero Cloud only.

docs.title: 3. File Actions
docs.text:
The ⋯ button at the end of a file's row opens its menu.

The menu of a Robot System, as a manager sees it Item Shown to Does Copy link Everyone Copies the project's link; a file has no page of its own Add to favorites Everyone Lists the file under Favorites on Home Duplicate file Editors and managers Copies the file in the same project, for example jackal copy. A Station copy keeps its documents and apps. File details Everyone The file's information. Editors and managers can change its name, description and icon color here. Download local copy Managers Saves the file as an .sdr (Download a Local Copy) Move to trash Editors and managers Moves the file to Trash after you confirm. An active file is deactivated first, and a Station saves its data on the way down.

An official Sodero World cannot be duplicated. A World that uses official Sodero files is copied without them: add those assets to the copy again in Studio. To bring back a trashed file, restore it from Trash (Move to Trash, Restore and Delete).

docs.title: 4. How Robot Worlds and Robot Systems Work Together
docs.text:
The Robot Systems of a project drive the robots in the project's active Robot World. You do not enter any address.

  • One active World per project. A project can hold several Robot Worlds, but while one is active, the others cannot be activated (Another Robot World is already running in this project).
  • Active Stations connect automatically to the project's active World, including their camera and IMU gateways. A Station activated before the World connects once the World is up.
  • Robots are matched by name. A simulation gateway drives the robot set as its node's Robot name: the name of the robot's articulation prim in the World, for example jackal. Use one gateway per independently controlled robot or joint group, and avoid overlapping actuator ranges.
  • Projects stay apart. A Station never reaches a World in another project. Keep the World and the Robot Systems that drive it in the same project.

Step by step: Connect to the World.

docs.title: Libraries
docs.text:
Each project has a library: files shared with everyone who can open the project, such as .sdr files, design documents and scenes. Sodero Assets holds the robots, environments and documents that Sodero publishes.

Library Holds Who sees it Who adds, exports and deletes files A project's library Files shared with one project Everyone with access to the project The workspace's owner and admins, and members when Members can manage the Library is on Sodero Assets Robots, environments and documents published by Sodero Everyone Nobody: it is read-only

The Import file dialog and the Station's Load YAML dialog call a project's library Project Library. The dialog that uploads a document into a Station node calls it Workspace Library.

docs.title: 1. Open a Project's Library
docs.text:
1. Click Library in the left navigation bar. The Library window lists the projects you can open in the current workspace; Search projects… filters them.
  2. Click a project. Its files are listed with their Name, Type, Size and the date they were Added. An .sdr file shows what it holds: Robot System or Robot World.
  3. To find a file, use Search files…, the type filter (All types) and the sort button (newest or oldest first). The back arrow returns to the list of projects.

A project whose library is empty shows Upload a file to share it with this project.

Add file, and the Export and Delete buttons of each file, are shown to the workspace's owner and admins, and to members when the owner has turned on Members can manage the Library (Change Workspace Settings). Export saves a copy of the file on your computer.

In a Station, Libraries › Project Library in the Station menu (the Sodero mark at the top left) opens the library of the Station's project.

docs.title: 2. Add Files
docs.text:
1. Open the project's library and click Add file.
  2. Drag a file onto the dialog, or click Choose file.
  3. Click Add file. The portal confirms Added NAME.
The library of Warehouse Demo

A file can be up to 2 GiB.

docs.title: 3. Use Library Files
docs.text: File Where you use it .sdr Import on the project page, on the Project Library tab, creates a Robot System or Robot World from it (Import an .sdr File) Gateway and robot documents (.gw, .sdd, .sddm, .sdda), camera settings, map bundles In the Station, when you upload a node's document (Documents and Settings) Graph files (.yaml) In the Station, with Load YAML (Load and Export the Graph) Scenes and assets (.usd, .usda, .usdc) In Studio, to build a World (Studio)

docs.title: 4. Delete Library Files
docs.text:
Click the file's Delete button.

Deleting a library file removes it at once; it does not go to Trash. Export a copy first if you may need the file again.

docs.title: 5. Sodero Assets
docs.text:
Sodero Assets is the content that Sodero publishes for everyone: robots, grounds, lighting and sky images for Studio, and robot and gateway documents for Manipulator, Mobile and Legged robots in the Station.

Sodero Assets are read-only, and you can view, edit and simulate them only in Sodero. A World that uses them keeps them in Sodero: its local copy and its duplicates leave them out. An official Sodero World cannot be downloaded or duplicated.

docs.title: 6. Storage Limits
docs.text: Your workspace's plan limits how much the project libraries can hold. Billing & Usage shows the Project libraries and Workspace storage meters (Billing and Usage). A file that does not fit is refused with a message that names the limit, such as Not enough room in the project libraries: …: delete files you no longer need, or contact Sodero.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text: A project holds the Robot Systems and Robot Worlds that belong together and decides who can open them. Every project belongs to a workspace.

docs.title: 1. The Project List
docs.text:
Click Projects in the left navigation bar. The portal also opens here after you sign in.

The project list of Acme Robotics

Each row shows the project's name and description, its Contents (for example 1 System · 1 World), its Members, My access (your role) and Last modified. A star marks a favorite, and a green Running badge shows while a file of the project is active.

Click a project to open it. The ⋯ button at the end of a row opens the project menu:

Item Shown to Does Manage access Managers Invites people, changes roles and sets the project access (Share and Collaborate) Add to favorites Everyone Lists the project under Favorites on Home Duplicate project Managers Copies the project Project settings Managers Name, description and project information Move to trash Managers Moves the project to Trash

docs.title: 2. Create a Project
docs.text:
1. On the project list, click + Project. A workspace without projects also offers Create new project.
  2. Enter a Name (up to 20 characters) and, if you like, a Description (up to 40 characters).
  3. Choose the Project access: Restricted (Invited people only, the default) or Workspace (All members of this workspace).
  4. Click Create. The new project opens.
The Create project dialog
  • If + Project is dimmed, only the workspace's owner and admins can create projects there. The owner can turn on Members can create projects (Workspaces and People).
  • Your workspace's plan limits how many projects the workspace can hold; projects in Trash do not count (Billing and Usage).

docs.title: 3. The Project Page
docs.text:
Click a project on the list to open it. The top bar shows Projects (back to the list), the project's name and your access.

Warehouse Demo, with the Robot System jackal and the Robot World warehouse Control Does Project VPN Connects your computer to the project's Stations (Project VPN) AI agents Shows how to connect an AI agent, and the project link to give it (AI Agents) Search files, Filters Show only the files whose name contains a text, or of one type or state Import Creates a file from an .sdr file (Import an .sdr File) New file Creates a Robot System or a Robot World (Create a File)

Editors and managers also see the selection bar under the toolbar (0 selected · Worlds: 0/1, Clear, Actions), which handles several files at once.

The files are listed in two tables, Robot Systems and Robot Worlds. Each row shows the file's Activation and Running state, the Actions links that open it, a Station's IP address, Auto off, Active users, Resource use and Last modified (Activate and Run). Clicking a row selects the file; files open only from their Actions links. The ⋯ button at the end of a row holds the file actions.

docs.title: 4. Project Access and Roles
docs.text:
Project access decides who can open the project: only the people invited to it (Restricted, the default), or also every member of the workspace (Workspace). Managers change it in Manage access (Share and Collaborate).

Each person in a project has one of three roles, shown in lists as Manager, Editor and Viewer:

  • Can manage, for people who look after the project: access, copies, downloads and Trash.
  • Can edit, for people who build and run the Robot Systems and Robot Worlds.
  • Can view, for people who look and review without changing anything.

The person who created a project can manage it, and so can the workspace's owner and admins.

Action Can view Can edit Can manage Open the project; see its files, their Activation state and active users ✓ ✓ ✓ See the Running state of an active file — ✓ ✓ Open Station · Edit, Station · Live, Studio and Theater view only ✓ ✓ Create, import, duplicate, rename and trash files — ✓ ✓ Activate, run, stop and deactivate files; change Auto off — ✓ ✓ Download a local copy of a file — — ✓ Invite people, change roles, set the project access — — ✓ Duplicate the project, change its settings, move it to Trash — — ✓ Restore or permanently delete the project's items in Trash — — ✓

Controls you cannot use are dimmed and give the reason on hover. Creating projects, managing project libraries and Empty all trash depend on your workspace role.

docs.title: Rename or Describe a Project
docs.text: Open the project's ⋯ menu, choose Project settings, change Project Name (up to 20 characters) or Description, and click Save.

docs.title: Duplicate a Project
docs.text:
Choose ⋯ › Duplicate project. The copy, for example Warehouse Demo copy, is created in the same workspace, with the same description and project access.

  • Every Robot System and Robot World is copied with its files. Each Station copy keeps its documents and its apps.
  • Official Sodero Worlds, and the official Sodero files that other Worlds use, are left out. A message names them.
  • Check Manage access on the copy and invite the people who need it.
  • The copy counts toward your plan's project limit.

docs.title: 6. Download a Local Copy
docs.text:
Managers can keep a Robot System or Robot World outside Sodero: open the file's ⋯ menu on the project page and choose Download local copy. The browser saves an .sdr file named after the file, for example jackal.sdr. To keep a whole project, download each of its files.

Use the copy to keep a backup, to import it into another project, or to move a Robot System to Stellar X (Move Robot Systems Between Stellar X and Sodero Cloud).

Tip: A Station saves its data when it deactivates. Deactivate the Robot System before you download it, so that the copy holds your latest changes.

Official Sodero content stays in Sodero. An official Sodero World cannot be downloaded, and a World that uses official Sodero files is downloaded without them.

docs.title: 7. Move to Trash, Restore and Delete
docs.text:
To move a project to Trash, open its ⋯ menu on the project list, choose Move to trash and confirm. Its active files are deactivated first, which ends their use of credits.

Click Trash in the left navigation bar to see the trashed projects, Robot Systems and Robot Worlds. The ⋯ menu of an entry, shown to the people who can manage it, offers:

  • Restore, which puts it back. Restoring a project needs room under your plan's project limit.
  • Delete permanently, which removes it for good. This cannot be undone.

Workspace owners and admins also have Empty all trash: after asking, it permanently deletes every entry they can manage.

Library files do not go to Trash. Deleting a file from a project's library removes it at once (Libraries).

docs.title: Share and Collaborate
docs.text: Work on a project with other people: invite them with a role, send them the project link and see who is working where. Sharing is set per project; membership of the workspace itself is covered in Workspaces and People.

docs.title: 1. Invite People
docs.text:
Managers invite people from the project list:

  1. Open the project's ⋯ menu and choose Manage access.
  2. Under Invite people, type an email address, or pick one of the workspace members it suggests.
  3. Choose the role: Can manage, Can edit (the default) or Can view (Project Access and Roles).
  4. Click Invite. The invitation goes out at once.
The Manage access dialog

The person receives an email titled Sodero project access: Warehouse Demo with a Review access button. The invitation is valid for 7 days; inviting the same address again replaces it. If the dialog says Couldn't send invitation. Try again., check the address: the person may already have access.

docs.title: Change Roles, Remove People, Set the Access
docs.text:
People with access lists everyone in the project with their role.

  • To change a role, use the person's role menu. To remove someone, click × on their row.
  • Project access at the top of the dialog switches between Restricted and Workspace.
  • Click Save to apply these changes. Cancel drops them; invitations already sent stay.

You cannot change your own role, and a project always keeps at least one manager.

docs.title: 2. Accept an Invitation
docs.text: The invited person clicks Review access in the email, signs in with the address the invitation was sent to and clicks Accept invitation. To decline, they ignore the email. Details and messages: Accept an Invitation.

docs.title: 3. Guests
docs.text: People invited to a project without being members of its workspace join it as guests. They find the project in the workspace menu under Switch workspace › Guest projects (N) (Guest Projects). Inside the project, a guest has the role they were invited with, like anyone else.

docs.title: 4. Send the Project Link
docs.text:
Every project has a link that opens it in the portal. Copy it with Manage access › Copy link, with a file's ⋯ › Copy link, with AI agents › Copy project link, or from the browser's address bar.

The link opens the project only for people who are signed in and have access to it, so invite new people first. The same applies to the link icon next to an active file's Station · Live or Theater link, which copies the address of that live view.

docs.title: 5. See Who Is Working
docs.text:
The Active users column of the project page shows who is working in each file right now. Click the avatars for each person's name, role and activity:

Activity The person is Station Design Editing the Station in Station · Edit Station open Working in Station · Live Recent Station API activity Using the Station through an AI agent or the Project VPN Theater viewer Watching the World in Theater Studio collaboration Editing the World in Studio

For recent activity in the whole workspace, such as projects created or files started and stopped, see Notifications.

docs.title: 6. Work Together on One Station or World
docs.text:
Several people can work in the same file at the same time:

  • Station. Everyone who opens a Robot System works on the same Station.
  • Studio. Everyone who opens a World in Studio joins the same editing session (Studio).
  • Theater. Everyone who opens an active World watches the same simulation, each in their own rendering mode. Each viewer can use credits while Theater is open (Billing and Usage).

People with Can view can look but not change anything. For example, Go live is disabled for them in Station · Edit.

Tip: Agree on who activates, runs, stops and deactivates a shared file. These actions change the file for everyone working in it.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Sodero Cloud and Stellar X share the robot-system concepts and the document types. Each product runs its own release of Stellar Station, so their Store apps, menus, node names and accepted document versions can differ.

docs.title: Robot Documents and Apps
docs.text:
Use gateway and robot documents (.gw, .sdd, .sddm, .sdda) made for the Station release you work with, such as the documents in Sodero Assets. The Station refuses a document in two cases:

  • An older format. The message says that the file uses an obsolete format, or names an Obsolete robot file or an Obsolete gateway filename (Documents in an Obsolete Format).
  • A robot document without runtime.yaml. Robot documents (.sdd, .sddm, .sdda) must contain a runtime.yaml that names their controller. Without it, the message says The robot document has no runtime.yaml naming its controller.

Documents exported from a current Stellar Designer meet both rules: export older documents again and upload the new file. Do not edit the files inside a document to make a Station accept it.

Install the apps that your nodes run from the Station's Store before you start the nodes (Apps and Packages).

docs.title: Move Files Between Products
docs.text:
An .sdr file carries a Robot System between Sodero Cloud and Stellar X, without its installed packages. Check the destination's Station release and apps before you import it (Move Robot Systems Between Stellar X and Sodero Cloud).

The Stellar X manual describes the Station on the controller. Use it for the concepts and the device steps; this manual's menus, such as Store, Station · Edit, Go live and Station · Live, apply to Sodero Cloud.

docs.title: Example Files
docs.text:
• The Quick Start scene jackal_warehouse.zip contains a Clearpath Jackal and a Clearpath Dingo with their license notice. Keep the license file with the scene when you pass it on.
  • The Quick Start's jackal.gw and jackal.sddm are the simulation gateway document and the mobile robot document of that Jackal, made for the Station release of Sodero Cloud.

docs.title: Browser and Rendering
docs.text: Use an up-to-date desktop browser. WebGPU needs support from the browser, the operating system and the GPU; when it is not available on your device, use RTX Real-time, which renders in the cloud and streams the picture (Choose Rendering Mode).

docs.title: External Tools
docs.text:
• Project VPN: install the Connector with the command for your operating system under Install Connector in the project's Project VPN panel, then sign in once with sodero login (Project VPN).
  • AI agents: connect them with the address and settings of the project's AI agents panel (AI Agents).

Your workspace's plan sets further limits, such as storage and how many Robot Systems and Robot Worlds can be active at once: Billing & Usage shows them (Set by Your Plan).

docs.title: Set by Your Plan
docs.text:
Your workspace's plan sets these limits. Billing & Usage, in the workspace menu, shows each one with what the workspace uses (Billing and Usage):

  • credits, their hourly rates and when they renew;
  • Projects in the workspace;
  • Workspace storage and Project libraries;
  • Systems and Worlds running at once;
  • AI agent (MCP) tool calls, Project VPN time and Project VPN data per calendar month;
  • AI agent tool calls per minute, when the plan limits them (Agents can make up to N tool calls per minute.).

Plans differ, so this manual gives no values for them. To change the plan or add credits, contact Sodero.

docs.title: Apps and Packages
docs.text:
Every node of a Station runs an app or module that is installed on that Station. Add node offers only what is installed, plus empty drafts. Apps come from the Store; your own programs are uploaded as module packages. Both are kept with the Robot System and installed each time its Station starts.

Source What it is Badge in Add node Where you install it Store app A program published by Sodero, such as the actuator gateway or a robot controller SODERO Store in the left rail Your own module A module package (.tar.gz) that you built CUSTOM Modules › Add custom module, or Package on the Live page

docs.title: 1. Starting Apps
docs.text:
When you create a Robot System, Starting apps offers bundles of Store apps, for example for a manipulator or a mobile robot. Empty has none (Create a File). The apps of the chosen bundle are recorded with the Robot System and install when the Station first starts.

A bundle is a starting point, not a complete system. Before you add nodes, check in the Store that every app your nodes run, such as the actuator gateway and the robot's controller, shows Installed.

If Add node lists only Empty gateway, Empty controller and the other drafts, no app is installed yet. Install the apps you need from the Store.

docs.title: 2. The Store
docs.text:
Click Store in the left rail. The Store lists the apps that Sodero publishes, one row each.

The Store of a new Robot System, on the Edit page Part of a row Shows Name The app and a short description, for example Gateway Designer (Gateway control and setup workspace) Included Every Store app is included in Sodero Cloud; there is nothing to buy State Not Installed or Installed Versions Current (the Store's release), Installed version, New when a newer release is out, and Installed (the date). An installed app also lists its Cloud permissions: what its own UI may use in Sodero Cloud, such as your profile or the project library. Buttons Install or Uninstall, and Update when a newer release is out

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Click Install. When the app installs depends on the page:

  • Edit page: the app is recorded for the Robot System and installs when the Station starts.
  • Live page: the app installs at once and is recorded for the Station's later starts.

The app then appears in Add node, under the node type it declares, with the SODERO badge (Add a Node).

docs.title: Update
docs.text: Update (Update to …) replaces the installed release with the Store's current one. While a node of the app runs, the button is disabled (Stop its running instances to update it): stop those nodes first. On the Edit page, Update records the new release, which installs when the Station starts.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text: Uninstall removes the app from the Robot System. While a node of the app runs, the button is disabled. While the saved graph still has nodes of the app, it is refused with a message that names them: delete those nodes, then uninstall.

docs.title: The Modules Page
docs.text: Click Modules in the left rail. Used modules in this system lists the Station's modules with Name, Type, Publisher (Sodero or Custom), Version and Used by, the number of nodes that use each one. The ⋯ menu of a row offers Module info (version, publisher, source, size and the nodes that use it) and Remove module.

docs.title: Upload a Module Package
docs.text:
1. Click Add custom module.
  2. Drop one or more packages (.tar.gz or .tgz) on the dialog, or click to choose them.
  3. Click Add module (Add N modules for several).

On the Live page, Package in the toolbar does the same from the graph: choose one or more packages, and they upload one after another (Uploading 1/2 · …).

As with Store apps, a package uploaded on the Edit page installs when the Station starts, and one uploaded on the Live page installs at once. Either way it is kept with the Robot System. Your module then appears in Add node under the type it declares, with the CUSTOM badge.

How to build a module package is described in Create Custom Modules in the Stellar X manual. In Sodero Cloud:

  • Stations run on x86-64 computers. Build the native programs in your package for x86-64 (amd64).
  • Keep packages small. Every uploaded package is installed again each time the Station starts, so large packages make starting and stopping slower.

docs.title: Remove a Module
docs.text: Stop and delete the nodes that use the module, then choose ⋯ › Remove module in its row. The dialog says how many nodes still use it; click Remove to confirm.

docs.title: Documents and Settings
docs.text: Most nodes work from a document: a gateway runs a gateway document (.gw), a robot controller runs a robot document (.sdd, .sddm or .sdda). Some apps also have settings that you edit in the node's inspector. This page shows how to give a node its document, which kinds exist, and how to change settings. You can do all of this on the Edit page and on the Live page, while the node is stopped.

docs.title: 1. Choose or Upload a Document
docs.text:
Select the node. The Parameters section of its inspector has one field for each document the app reads, for example Gateway project on an actuator gateway or document (robot) on a controller.

The inspector of an actuator gateway, with its gateway document jackal and the Robot name under Parameters
  • A new node starts from a blank document. When you add an actuator gateway or a robot controller, the Station gives it a document named after the node that holds a blank template: for sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal, the document jackal with the file default.gw. A robot controller's template is default.sdd, default.sddm or default.sdda. Upload the document made for your robot in its place.
  • The dropdown lists the documents of that kind in the Station. A field that a controller requires reads Select a required document until it names one; other fields may offer Built-in default (no document). Built-in defaults do not describe your robot: give every gateway and controller the document made for it.
  • The line under the field tells which file the document holds, for example Uploaded: jackal.gw · 1.2 KB · …, or Not uploaded.
Button What it does Upload Brings in a new document (Upload a Document) Edit Opens the document in its editor in a new tab: the Gateway Designer for a gateway document, Stellar Designer for a robot document Delete Next to an uploaded file: puts the document back to its blank template. The Station asks first, for example Delete jackal.gw? The gateway-project document jackal becomes the blank template default.gw.

docs.title: Upload a Document
docs.text:
1. Click Upload under the field. The dialog is named after the kind, for example Upload gateway-project document or Upload robot document.

  2. Choose where the file comes from:

    Tab Files From your PC Drop the file on the dialog, or click Choose file Workspace Library The files of the project library (Libraries) Sodero Assets Robot and gateway documents published by Sodero, under Manipulator, Mobile and Legged. Only for robot and gateway documents.

  3. Click Import.

Uploading a gateway document from your PC The same dialog for a robot document

The Station confirms the upload, for example jackal.gw uploaded as the gateway-project document jackal, and the node takes the new document. If the upload fails, the message says why: … was not uploaded — ….

  • If the field already names a document, the upload replaces that document.
  • A new document is named after the last part of the node name: for sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal it is jackal (Name the Node).

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• A running node is locked. While a node runs, its inspector says This node is running. Stop it to change its documents, parameters, settings, ports or name. Stop the node before you upload, edit or delete its document or change its settings.
  • Each controller takes its own kind: .sdd for sodero.mmc, .sddm for sodero.mlc, .sdda for sodero.amc.
  • A robot document names its gateway and the gateway's actuators it uses. Connect the controller's servo_link to that gateway, and give the gateway at least as many actuators as the document uses.

docs.title: 2. Kinds of Documents
docs.text:
Kind File Used by Gateway document .gw Actuator gateways, sodero.actuator_gateway.<name> Robot document .sdd (manipulator), .sddm (mobile base), .sdda (articulated robot) sodero.mmc.<name>, sodero.mlc.<name>, sodero.amc.<name> Tool bank, Pose bank .tool, .pose, exported from Motion Studio The manipulator controller sodero.mmc.<name>, in its Tool bank and Pose bank fields. Motion Studio edits them in place. Camera document .yaml Camera gateways, sodero.camera_gateway.<name> IMU document imu.yaml, created in the node's settings IMU gateways, sodero.imu_gateway.<name> GNSS document A gateway document that holds gnss.yaml, created in the node's settings GNSS gateways, sodero.gnss_gateway.<name> Map bundle A .nav folder packed as .tar.gz, .tgz, .tar or .zip, for example site.nav.tgz The localizer, the navigator and visual odometry

A Station has one map bundle: the localizer, the navigator and visual odometry share it, and a new upload replaces it. What a map bundle holds is described in Load and Configure a Map in the Stellar X manual.

docs.title: 3. Settings
docs.text:
Some apps declare settings. The inspector then shows one section per settings file below Parameters, titled by the app.

  1. Stop the node if it runs.
  2. Change the fields.

  3. Click Save settings (Settings saved.). Discard and reload discards your changes.

  4. When the settings belong to a document, the section shows once the node has one: Choose or upload a … document in Parameters; its … settings then appear here.

  5. Some apps can create the file for you: click Create with defaults. An IMU or GNSS gateway without a document creates one here: enter a name under New … document and click Create.
  6. The fields themselves come from each app.

docs.title: 4. Make Documents in Stellar Designer
docs.text:
Gateway and robot documents are made in Stellar Designer: the Gateway Designer makes .gw documents, and the manipulator, mobile robot and articulation editors make .sdd, .sddm and .sdda documents. Edit in the inspector opens a node's document there. Every editor and field is described in the Stellar X manual: Stellar Designer and Gateway Designer.

  • The robot that a simulation gateway drives in the World is set on the gateway node, as its Robot name (Connect to the World).
  • Ready-made documents for Sodero's robots are in Sodero Assets.

docs.title: Documents in an Obsolete Format
docs.text: Documents from an older Stellar Designer use an obsolete format, and the Station refuses them: the message says that the file uses an obsolete format, or names an Obsolete robot file or an Obsolete gateway filename. A robot document without runtime.yaml, the file that names its controller, is refused the same way: The robot document has no runtime.yaml naming its controller. Export the document again from the current Stellar Designer and upload the new file.
