docs.title: Build the Graph
docs.text: A Station is a graph of nodes connected through ports. This page shows how to add and name nodes, connect them, and keep a large graph tidy. You can change the graph on the Edit page and on the Live page; every change is saved automatically. The node types are explained in Key Concepts.

docs.title: 1. Add a Node
docs.text:
1. Click Add node in the toolbar, or right-click the empty canvas.

  2. Choose the node type: Gateway, Controller, Compound or Application.

    Choosing the node type

  3. Under Select a module, choose the app or module, then click Next.

    Gateway › sodero.actuator_gateway

  4. Enter the node name and click Add node. You can rename the node later.

    Naming the node

The node appears on the canvas as Planned. Nothing runs until you start it on the Live page (Start and Monitor Nodes).

docs.title: The Module List
docs.text:
Badge Entry Detail line SODERO An app installed from the Store Sodero package · and its version CUSTOM A module package you uploaded Imported package · Installed DRAFT Empty gateway, Empty controller, Empty compound, Empty application Empty subsystem to develop yourself (no package): a placeholder with no program behind it, for sketching a system. It does not start.

Each type lists only the apps and modules installed on this Station. To add another, install it first (Apps and Packages).

docs.title: Name the Node
docs.text:
The name field proposes the app's own name, for example sodero.actuator_gateway. Add a last part that names the robot or device, so that the name reads sodero.<package>.<name>:

Node Example name Actuator gateway of a robot sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal Mobile base controller of the same robot sodero.mlc.jackal Manipulator controller sodero.mmc.arm Articulation controller sodero.amc.dog Strider sodero.strider
  • The last part names the node's documents. A new document you upload to sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal is named jackal (Documents and Settings).
  • Robot documents refer to their gateway by its node name, for example sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal. Give the gateway the name its controller's document expects.
  • Give a robot's gateway and controller the same last part. The graph stays easy to read.
  • Names use letters, digits, _, . and -, start with a letter or digit, and have up to 60 characters (an empty draft: 20). Each name can be used once per Station: … is already a node of this graph: use another id, e.g. ….2.

docs.title: 2. Node Cards
docs.text:
Part Meaning Title The node name Second line The app or module the node runs REQUIRES n/m Ports the node needs from other nodes, on the left edge of the card: connected / total PROVIDES n/m Ports the node offers, on the right edge: ports with at least one connection / total State Planned until the node first starts, then its running state (Node States)

The card border has the color of the node type: orange for gateways, blue-violet for controllers, purple for compounds and mint for applications. The arrow at the top right of a card folds its ports away.

docs.title: 3. Connect Ports
docs.text:
Connect a port that one node requires to a matching port that another node provides:

  • Drag from one port dot to the other.
  • Click one port, then the other.
  • In the inspector of the node that requires the port, click Auto-connect next to the port. The Station connects the first matching port it finds, or shows No match.

The Station accepts a connection only when the two ports are on different nodes, one requires and the other provides, and both use the same interface. The inspector shows each port's interface under its name, for example api.actuator.servo.v1. The Station also keeps the system's structure:

  • Only a controller may use a gateway.
  • An application uses controllers or compounds, never gateways directly.
  • One controller drives a gateway.

A refused connection says why, for example Connect ports on different nodes with opposite directions and matching contracts.

To remove a connection, select the node and click Disconnect next to the port in the inspector.

Check Auto-connect with several robots. Auto-connect does not look at node names: with two gateways in the graph, it may pick the other robot's. Check the result, or drag the connection yourself.

docs.title: Common Connections
docs.text:
Node (requires) Port Connect to (provides) sodero.mmc.<name>, sodero.mlc.<name>, sodero.amc.<name> servo_link The robot's actuator gateway sodero.actuator_gateway.<name>, port servo_link sodero.strider mobile_base The mobile base controller sodero.mlc.<name>, port mobile_base sodero.strider localization The localizer sodero.icp_localizer, port localization sodero.strider navigation The navigator sodero.navigator, port navigation sodero.icp_localizer camera (required) The robot's camera gateway sodero.camera_gateway.<name>, port camera sodero.navigator mobile_base The mobile base controller sodero.mlc.<name>, port mobile_base sodero.navigator localization The localizer sodero.icp_localizer, port localization

Strider drives what its ports are connected to (Strider).

For navigation, install sodero.icp_localizer and sodero.navigator from the Store (Apps and Packages) and add them. The localizer needs its camera port connected; the navigator drives the base connected to its mobile_base port and follows the robot's position from the localizer connected to its localization port. Both read the Station's map bundle (Documents and Settings).

docs.title: 4. Rename and Delete
docs.text:
• Rename: click the pencil next to the node name in the inspector and enter the new name. The node keeps its connections and the documents it uses.
  • Delete: right-click the node and choose Delete node. The dialog asks Delete "…" from this robot system?; click Delete node. The node's connections are removed too.

On the Live page, stop a node before you rename or delete it.

Deleting a node cannot be undone. Everyone working on the Station sees the change at once.

docs.title: 5. Find Your Way in a Large Graph
docs.text:
• Filter shows only nodes of one Node type or Status; Reset all clears it.
  • Fit view zooms to show every node; Auto layout arranges the nodes by their connections.
  • The N issues chip at the left of the toolbar lists problems, such as Required port "servo_link" is not connected. Locate jumps to the node.

docs.title: 6. Load and Export the Graph
docs.text:
• Export downloads the graph as a .yaml file. If something runs on the Live page that the graph does not show, it asks first: Planned topology only or Also include what is running.
  • Load YAML loads such a file from your PC (From your PC) or from the project library (Project Library). It replaces the nodes and connections of the Station (… loaded — N nodes now in the system.).

The file holds the graph only: nodes, their parameters and their connections. Documents, settings and apps are not part of it. To copy a whole Robot System, use Duplicate file, or Download local copy and Import, on the project page (Robot Systems and Robot Worlds).

docs.title: Stellar Station
docs.text: Every Robot System is one Stellar Station ("the Station"). In the Station you build the robot system as a graph of nodes, give the nodes their documents, start them, and watch their state and logs.

docs.title: What a Robot System Is
docs.text:
A Robot System holds one Station and everything it needs:

Part What it is Node graph Gateways, controllers, compounds and applications, and the connections between their ports (Build the Graph) Documents and settings Gateway and robot documents, camera files, map bundles and node settings (Documents and Settings) Apps and modules The Store apps and your own module packages that the nodes run (Apps and Packages)

A Robot System drives robots in the project's active Robot World (Connect to the World). You create it on the project page (Robot Systems and Robot Worlds). Nodes, ports and node types are explained in Key Concepts.

docs.title: 1. Open the Station
docs.text:
On the project page, the Robot System's Actions column holds the link:

  • Station · Edit while the Robot System is inactive. It opens the Edit page.
  • Station · Live while it is active. It opens the Live page; opening it does not start any node.

The Station opens in a new browser tab and uses your portal sign-in. The header shows the project and the Robot System, for example Warehouse Demo / jackal. People with Can view can open both pages, but every control that changes something is disabled for them (Project Access and Roles).

docs.title: Edit and Live
docs.text:
The Station has two pages for the same Robot System:

Edit page Live page Badge EDIT LIVE, with how long the Station has been live The Station Inactive: nothing runs and no credits are used Active: it uses credits (Billing and Usage) What you can do Add, connect, rename and delete nodes; give them their documents and settings; select Store apps The same, while the nodes concerned are stopped; start and stop nodes, read their logs and open the operator UIs Button Go live Stop live The Edit page of a new Robot System
  • Go live activates the Station, like Active in the portal's Activation column. A banner follows the start, and Cancel stops it. When the Station is ready, usually after about a minute, the tab moves on to the Live page by itself.
  • Stop live asks first: Every node stops and the system goes back to edit mode. Nodes and connections stay saved. It deactivates the Station, like Deactivate in the portal, and the tab returns to the Edit page.
  • When someone else activates the Station while you are on the Edit page, your tab moves on to the Live page as well.

docs.title: 2. Screen Layout
docs.text:
Area Contents Header Project and Robot System, the EDIT or LIVE badge, Go live or Stop live, Resources, and the people who have the Station open Left rail Runtime (the graph), Modules and Store (Apps and Packages); at the bottom Notifications, Help and your account Toolbar The save state (Saved), Filter, Load YAML, Export and Add node. The Live page adds Package and Start all nodes, and Adopt running when something runs that the graph does not show. The last button shows or hides the inspector. Canvas The node cards and their connections. At the bottom: zoom, Fit view, Auto layout, and folding or unfolding all cards. Inspector The selected node: name, module and state, Connection, Parameters and settings, Logs (Live page only) and Activity

The Sodero mark at the top left opens the Station menu: Back to Sodero Cloud, Libraries › Project Library, Theme (Midnight or Twilight), Help & Feedback and About Stellar Station. Project Library opens the project library: the files that everyone in the project shares, such as documents and graph files (Libraries).

Tip: Right-click the empty canvas to add a node, and right-click a node for its actions.

docs.title: 3. What Is Saved Where
docs.text:
What Where it is kept Changes to the graph Saved automatically on both pages. The toolbar shows Saving…, then Saved; if a save fails, it shows Retry save. Changes made on the Live page stay after Stop live. Documents and settings With the Robot System, whether you give them on the Edit page or on the Live page. The Station saves them when it is deactivated and restores them when it is activated (Documents and Settings). Store apps and your modules Recorded with the Robot System and installed each time the Station starts (Apps and Packages) The whole Robot System Download local copy on the project page saves it as an .sdr file (Download a Local Copy)

Export in the toolbar saves the graph only, not the documents or apps (Load and Export the Graph).

docs.title: 4. Resources
docs.text:
Click Resources in the header to see the Station's CPU, RAM and GPU load. The bars turn amber at 70 % and red at 85 %. — means that no value is reported; on the Edit page every value is — (Usage appears once the system is live.). View details opens the system monitor.

Sodero Cloud gives each Station its own share of CPU and memory. The project page also shows the Station's use in its Resource column; hover over it for the Station's CPUs and its memory limit (The Project Page). When a Station runs close to its limits, give it fewer nodes, for example by putting each robot in its own Robot System.

docs.title: 5. What You Do on the Station
docs.text:
flowchart LR
 A["Select apps"] --> B["Add and connect nodes"]
 B --> C["Give the nodes their documents"]
 C --> D["Connect to the World"]
 D --> E["Go live and start nodes"]
 E --> F["Open the operator UI"]
Step Page Install the apps that your nodes run Apps and Packages Add nodes and connect their ports Build the Graph Give the nodes their documents and settings Documents and Settings Name the robots and match their joints to the World Connect to the World Go live, run the World, start nodes, read their state and logs Start and Monitor Nodes Drive and teach the robots Strider, Motion Studio, Articulation

The Quick Start builds and runs a World. Its last section, Next: Connect a Robot System, and the pages above take you on to a Robot System that drives a robot in that World.

docs.title: Start and Monitor Nodes
docs.text: Nodes run only on the Live page, and only when you start them. This page covers starting and stopping nodes, reading their state and logs, and what to do when a node does not start.

docs.title: 1. Go Live
docs.text:
Open the Robot System with Station · Edit and click Go live, or activate it on the project page and open Station · Live (Edit and Live). The Station comes up with its saved graph, documents and apps, but no node starts by itself: nodes that have not run yet show Planned.

Starting and stopping nodes needs the Can edit or Can manage role in the project.

docs.title: 2. Start All Nodes
docs.text:
Click Start all nodes in the toolbar. The Station starts every node that is not running, in dependency order: Nodes start in dependency order: gateway → controller → compound → application. A node waits until the nodes it requires are up.

  • A banner follows the progress. Cancel start stops the run; nodes that already started stay up.
  • The result shows as a banner: Runtime topology is up., or Runtime topology is up; stopped during startup: … when some nodes stopped again (Troubleshooting).
  • The arrow next to the button opens its menu: Start all nodes and Stop all nodes.
  • Nothing in this topology can be launched from here. means that the graph holds only empty drafts.

Run on the project page does the same for a Robot System, and can start a World and several Stations in one step (Run and Stop).

docs.title: 3. Start, Restart or Stop One Node
docs.text:
Right-click a node on the Live page:

The menu of a running node Item Shown when Open … The node has a UI of its own, for example Strider or Motion Studio Start node The node is not running Restart node, Stop node The node runs Delete node Always (Rename and Delete)

Start a robot's nodes in order: the gateway first, then its controller, then the nodes that use the controller. Stop them in the reverse order.

The operator UIs that open from nodes are described in Strider, Motion Studio and Articulation.

docs.title: 4. Node States
docs.text:
The footer of each node card and the inspector header show the node's state, and the inspector adds a short description.

State Description Planned Not started yet. Booting, Starting Starting up. Waiting binding A required port has no connection yet. Waiting target Connected target is not ready yet. Ready Started and waiting to operate. Operating Running normally. Running, Active Process is up. Paused Paused. Idle Instance exists but is not running. Degraded Running with reduced performance. Disconnected Heartbeat lost. Fault Fault state — reset to recover. Error, Failed, Crashed The node reported an error. Stopped, Exited Process ended.

The dot next to the state is green while the node runs, yellow while it waits, red for errors and grey otherwise. Problems are also counted in the N issues chip of the toolbar.

Waiting binding means that the node runs, but a port it requires is not connected to a running node that provides it. Connect the port, and start the providing node first: the gateway before its controller. When the two ports do not fit together, the inspector shows the reason instead of the description.

docs.title: 5. Logs and Activity
docs.text:
On the Live page, the Logs section of the inspector shows the node's latest output. Choose a stream and click Refresh:

Stream Contents Package log The app's own log Standard output, Standard error The program's output Node log (userdata) The node's log file Process log When the process started and stopped Gateway events A gateway's status and problems. A controller shows the events of its gateway as Gateway events (…).

Each stream shows its last 200 lines and when it was last updated, for example Last 200 lines · updated 5 s ago.

  • Station packages are still being restored; this node may not start yet. The Station is still installing its apps after going live. Wait a moment, then start the node.
  • Package restore at Station start failed: … The node's app could not be installed (Apps and Packages).

Activity, under the logs, lists the latest changes to the node and who made them. The Notifications bell in the left rail lists the Station's recent events: nodes added, connected and deleted, files uploaded, and on the Live page also nodes started and stopped, and errors.

docs.title: 6. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Message What to do … did not start: … The app ended at once; the text after the colon is its own reason. Details shows more, and Copy copies it. Fix the cause, often the document or a setting, then start again. … cannot start yet: connect the … port or set … The app needs that port connected, or that parameter set in Parameters. Do one of the two, then start again. Install the package of … (…) from the Store first. Nothing was started. The node's app is not installed on this Station (Apps and Packages) Provider not ready: … or Requirements never bound A node that it requires did not come up. Start that node first and read its log. Process exited before reaching readiness or Timed out waiting for readiness The node stopped or hung while starting. Read its logs. Process stopped during topology startup; check its logs before retrying. The node started, then stopped. Read its logs, fix the cause, then start again. Gateway … cannot be driven by both … and …; choose one controller before starting all nodes. Two controllers are connected to one gateway. Disconnect one of them. Project edit access is required to start or cancel the topology. Your role is Can view. Ask a manager for Can edit.

A gateway that cannot reach its robot in the World does not fail: it waits. See Connect to the World.

docs.title: 7. Stop
docs.text:
To Do this The Station Stop one node Right-click it › Stop node Stays live Stop every node Choose Stop all nodes in the menu of Start all nodes (users of a node stop before the node itself), or Stop on the project page Stays live and keeps using credits End your session Stop live in the Station, or Deactivate on the project page Stops every node, saves its data and returns to the Edit page. It no longer uses credits.

Stop live and Deactivate do the same. If nobody uses an active Station, Auto off deactivates it after 30 minutes by default (Auto Off).

Stopping this Station does not stop or deactivate its World, and does not end separate rendering sessions. End those from the project page and close unneeded views.

docs.title: Connect to the World
docs.text:
The Robot Systems of a project drive the robots in the project's active Robot World. Sodero Cloud makes the connection: a simulation gateway reaches the World by itself and finds its robot by name. This page shows what to set so that a robot moves.

flowchart LR
    subgraph RS ["Robot System"]
        C["Controller<br>sodero.mlc.jackal"] -- servo_link --> G["Simulation gateway<br>sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal<br>Robot name: jackal"]
    end
    subgraph W ["Robot World, active"]
        R["Robot prim jackal<br>joints 1 to 4"]
    end
    G -- "found by name" --> R

docs.title: 1. What Is Automatic
docs.text:
• No address to set. The simulation, camera and IMU gateways of an active Station reach the project's active World through the local simulator address, which is the default in their documents: Sodero Cloud forwards it to the World. Keep that default; a document that points to another address does not reach the World.
  • Activate in any order. A Station that is active before the World connects once the World is up.
  • One World per project. Only one Robot World of a project can be active at a time, and a Station never reaches a World in another project (How Robot Worlds and Robot Systems Work Together).

docs.title: 2. Name the Robot
docs.text:
A simulation gateway drives the robot whose articulation prim has its robot name. You set the robot name on the gateway node in the Station, so that one gateway document fits any robot:

  1. Select the simulation gateway node, for example sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal.
  2. Under Parameters, check that Gateway project names its gateway document (Documents and Settings).
  3. In Robot name, under the document, enter the name of the robot's articulation prim, for example jackal for /World/jackal. Press Enter, or leave the field, to save it.

A new name applies at the gateway's next start. Without a name, the inspector says No robot name yet: the gateway is tied to no robot in the World. Renaming the node does not change the robot it drives.

The robot name must be exactly the name of the robot's articulation prim in the World.

Station World Gateway node sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal with the Robot name jackal The robot's articulation prim jackal, at /World/jackal in the World's hierarchy
  • Names are case-sensitive: Jackal and jackal are different robots.
  • A robot name uses letters, digits and _, and does not start with a digit.
  • Every robot in the World needs a name of its own.

If the names differ, the gateway never finds its robot: it keeps waiting, and the robot does not move.

docs.title: 3. Match Actuators and Joints
docs.text:
The gateway addresses joints by actuator index. Actuator i drives the robot's i-th movable joint, revolute or prismatic, in the order of the robot's USD file; joints marked rc:passive = true are skipped (Prepare a World for Simulation).

Gateway Robot in the World Actuators 1, 2, 3, 4 (indices 0 to 3) The robot's 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th movable joint in USD order
  • Give the gateway one actuator per joint it drives. The robot document then maps the gateway's actuators to its joints or wheels (Documents and Settings).
  • The Joints list in Studio is alphabetical; it does not show this order.
  • To drive one robot with two gateways, for example an arm and its gripper, set the gripper gateway's DOF offset to the index of the gripper's first joint (Gateway Designer › Simulation Gateways in the Stellar X manual).

What a robot needs in the World, such as its articulation and joint drives, is described in Prepare a World for Simulation.

docs.title: 4. Several Robots and Stations
docs.text:
• Use one gateway and one controller per robot, each gateway with its own robot name.
  • The gateways can sit in one Robot System or in several. Every active Robot System of the project connects to the same World.
  • Drive each robot, or each part of a robot, from one gateway only.

docs.title: 5. Cameras and IMUs
docs.text:
• Camera gateway (sodero.camera_gateway.<name>): its camera name must be the name of the camera's prim in the World. It uses letters, digits, _, - and .. The World renders the robots' cameras while it is active; the first pictures can take a moment after the World starts.
  • IMU gateway (sodero.imu_gateway.<name>): it reads the IMU of one robot, which you name like the robot of an actuator gateway.

The World must declare its cameras and IMUs (Prepare a World for Simulation).

docs.title: 6. Start Order
docs.text: Activate the World and the Robot System and run the World (Activate and Run), start the gateway before its controller (Start and Monitor Nodes), then switch the servo on in the controller's UI (Strider, Motion Studio, Articulation).

docs.title: 7. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
A gateway connects to the World, not to another node. A World that is not running, or a robot name that does not match, therefore shows neither as Waiting binding nor as an error in the graph: the gateway's node can look normal while the gateway waits for its robot. Select the gateway and read its Gateway events log (Logs and Activity). It says whether the gateway is still waiting for its robot or is connected to the simulation.

Symptom What to check The gateway keeps waiting for its robot The World is active and playing; it is in the same project; the gateway's Robot name equals the robot's prim name exactly; the gateway document keeps the default simulator address The controller stays in Waiting binding Its servo_link is connected to the gateway, and the gateway runs (Node States) The servo switches on, but the robot does not move The gateway has as many actuators as the robot document uses. In Strider, the drive mode is Twist. A wheel or joint turns the wrong way, or the wrong joint moves Stop motion. Check the robot's joint order in USD, the actuator mapping of the robot document, the axis direction and the configured polarity. Change the document, then check one joint at a time. The servo switched off by itself The World may have been stopped or reset; stopping a World resets its robots' poses. Switch the servo on again. The camera gateway shows no picture The camera name equals the camera's prim name; the World plays and declares its cameras The robot moves slower than expected In Theater, Physics RTF is below 1.00: the World simulates slower than real time (Theater)

docs.title: Prepare a World for Simulation
docs.text:
The Stations of a project can drive a robot in its Robot World only when the World follows a few rules. They are the rules for a robot in NVIDIA Isaac Sim on Stellar X, plus two more: a purpose for robot cameras and a schema on fixed joints. The scene of the Quick Start follows all of them: use it as a model.

Studio has no tools to create articulations, joints, colliders or cameras. Prepare robots in a USD tool such as Isaac Sim (Prepare the Robot in the Stellar X manual), then bring the scene into the World with Replace scene…. A robot in a single USD file can also come in through Upload from PC (Studio).

docs.title: The Rules
docs.text: Rule Why The World is Z-up, in meters, and has a PhysicsScene. Studio refuses Y-up scenes, and the simulation needs a physics scene. Each robot is one articulation. Its top prim carries an Articulation Root. A robot is simulated and driven as one articulation. The prim name is the robot name. It is unique in the World and equals the Robot name set on the robot's simulation gateway node. A simulation gateway finds its robot by this name. Actuators follow the USD joint order. Actuator i of a gateway drives the robot's i-th movable joint in USD order. The gateway addresses joints by actuator index. Robot cameras have unique names and the purpose guide. A camera gateway reads its camera by name, and Sodero renders robot cameras that have this purpose. Fixed joints carry a physics joint schema. A fixed joint without one takes no part in the simulation.

docs.title: 1. Z-Up and a PhysicsScene
docs.text:
• Author the scene Z-up, in meters. Studio refuses a scene that declares Y-up: convert it before you bring it in.
  • Include a PhysicsScene prim. Check that the Hierarchy in Studio shows one; the Quick Start's scene does.

docs.title: 2. One Articulation per Robot
docs.text:
• The robot's top prim carries the Articulation Root. A robot has exactly one.
  • Its links are rigid bodies with colliders and realistic masses. Studio can correct a body's mass or density (Studio).
  • The prim's name is the robot name: letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit. It must be unique in the World, and case matters.
  • The robot's simulation gateway node uses the same name as its Robot name (Connect to the World). For the example scene, the Jackal articulation is /World/jackal.

Names must match. If the gateway node's Robot name differs from the robot's prim name, the robot never moves. Rename the prim, or change the Robot name.

docs.title: 3. Actuators Follow the USD Joint Order
docs.text:
A simulation gateway drives the robot's joints by actuator index:

  • Actuator 1 (index 0) drives the first movable joint under the robot prim, actuator 2 the second, and so on. Movable joints are revolute and prismatic joints; fixed joints are not actuators.
  • The order is the order in which the robot's USD file defines the joints, for example the order of the joint prims in a .usda file.
  • A joint marked rc:passive = true is not an actuator and is skipped.

The robot document maps its joints or wheels to the gateway's actuators: that mapping must match this order. Use robot documents prepared for this scene and Station release (Compatibility).

Studio's Joints (n) list shows a robot's joint names and their number, in alphabetical order: it does not show the actuator order.

Before normal operation, test one joint or wheel at a time with a small command and confirm that the intended part moves in the intended direction. Stop and correct the actuator mapping or axis configuration if it does not. Keep joint limits consistent with the robot model.

docs.title: 4. Cameras and IMUs
docs.text:
Cameras. A camera gateway reads one camera of the World by its name.

  • Put each robot camera, a Camera prim, under the link it is mounted on, so that it moves with the robot.
  • Give it a unique name. The camera gateway's camera name is this prim name: letters, digits, _, - and ..
  • Set the camera's purpose to guide. Robot cameras need this purpose in Sodero Cloud; a camera without it is not rendered for the Station.

While the World is active, Sodero renders its robot cameras for the camera gateways of the project's Stations. Theater's loading screen shows their progress under Robot cameras.

IMUs. An IMU gateway reads an IMU on a link of the robot. Declare it on the robot prim with rc:imuLink, the name of the link, and rc:imuOffset, its position on that link in meters, as for Isaac Sim (Prepare the Robot › IMU).

docs.title: 5. Fixed Joints
docs.text:
A fixed joint holds a body in place, for example the base of a manipulator on the world. Give every fixed joint a physics joint schema, such as PhysxJointAPI. Without one, the joint takes no part in the simulation in Sodero Cloud, and a fixed-base robot falls over.

In Isaac Sim, you can set a camera's purpose and a fixed joint's schema with Window › Script Editor, then save the scene:

import omni.usd
from pxr import PhysxSchema, UsdGeom

stage = omni.usd.get_context().get_stage()

# a robot camera: purpose guide
camera = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/my_robot/links/base_link/cam0")
UsdGeom.Imageable(camera).CreatePurposeAttr().Set(UsdGeom.Tokens.guide)

# the fixed joint that holds my_arm to the world: a physics joint schema
anchor = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/my_arm/joints/anchor")
PhysxSchema.PhysxJointAPI.Apply(anchor)

Replace the prim paths with those of your scene.

docs.title: 6. Keep the World Light
docs.text:
• Everything in the World is drawn, but only physics content takes part in the simulation: the physics scene, rigid bodies, colliders, joints and articulations. Give physics only to what the robots touch.
  • Large scenes take longer to load. Theater reports a World that has not loaded within 3 minutes. A file you bring into Studio can be up to 1 GiB.
  • Watch Physics RTF in Theater. Near 1.00, the simulation keeps up with real time; if it stays well below 1.00, make the World lighter.

docs.title: 7. Test the World in Theater
docs.text:
Check the World on its own before you connect Stations to it:

  1. Save the World in Studio and close Studio.
  2. On the project page, activate the World.
  3. Open Theater and wait until the World, and its Robot cameras if it has any, have loaded.
  4. Click Start Theater.
  5. Check that:
    • the robots rest on the ground and do not fall through it or drift away;
    • a fixed-base robot stays in place;
    • Physics RTF is near 1.00;
    • each robot appears in Scene assets under the Robot name of its gateway node.
  6. Click Stop Theater. To change the World, deactivate it and open it in Studio.

Next: Connect to the World.

docs.title: Studio
docs.text: Studio is the World editor of Sodero Cloud. In it you build a Robot World: bring in a scene or Sodero Assets, arrange the objects, set mass and joint poses, and save. Its browser tab is titled Cosmic Studio.

docs.title: 1. Open Studio
docs.text:
1. On the project page, click Studio in the Robot World's Actions column. Studio opens only while the World is Inactive (or in Error): deactivate an active World first.
  2. In Choose rendering mode, pick RTX Real-time or WebGPU and click Open Cosmic Studio (Choose Rendering Mode).

  3. Studio opens in a new tab once its editing session has started.

  4. The first time someone who can edit opens a new World, Studio adds a default environment from Sodero Assets: Lighting and Ground.

  5. A World with several top-level USD files asks which one to open.
  6. Keep the Sodero Cloud tab that opened Studio open while you work: Studio uses it to keep you signed in. If you close it, some actions say Open Cosmic Studio from Sodero Cloud to use this.

docs.title: The Studio Window
docs.text:
Studio with the warehouse World of the Quick Start Area What it holds Header The project and World names, the renderer menu (RTX Real-time ▾), the session time, the save state (Saved just now), Enter Theater ▾, Resources ▾ and the people in the session Left rail The Cosmic Studio menu (the logo), Scene, Save now, Undo, Redo, the asset libraries Workspace and Sodero Assets, and Grid Scene panel Filter scene, + to add a group or a light, and the Hierarchy of the World Viewport The World, with Perspective ▾ and View ▾ at the top left, the tools at the bottom, and the resolution and frame rate at the bottom right Asset detail The properties of the selected object. The panel button at the top right of the viewport shows and hides it.

The Cosmic Studio menu holds Back to Sodero Cloud (closes Studio), Libraries, World, Edit, Help & Feedback and About Cosmic Studio.

The World menu

docs.title: Replace the Whole Scene
docs.text:
Use it for a scene built elsewhere, for example in NVIDIA Isaac Sim.

  1. In the Cosmic Studio menu, choose World › Replace scene….
  2. On This PC, drag a USD file (.usd, .usda, .usdc), a USDZ package (.usdz) or a zipped USD folder (.zip) onto the dialog, or click Choose file. Workspace Library offers the USD files of the project library (Libraries).
  3. Click Replace and confirm in the browser's dialog.
  4. Studio says Replaced with …. Check the new scene in the Hierarchy, then click Save now.
The Replace scene dialog
  • The unsaved edits of everyone in the session are discarded.
  • A file can be up to 1 GiB. The scene must be Z-up: Studio refuses a Y-up scene (Prepare a World for Simulation).
  • In a zip, keep the scene's main USD file at the top level, with the files it uses beside it or below it. Studio opens the USD file nearest to the top of the zip.

docs.title: Add Sodero Assets
docs.text:
1. Click Sodero Assets in the left rail. The Asset Browser opens.
  2. Search by name, manufacturer, model or tags, filter with All kinds, All categories and All manufacturers, or browse the folders: environments, materials, objects, robots and scenes.
  3. Select the asset and check Parent prim (where it goes, /World by default) and Prim name (its name in the World).
  4. Click Add Reference (follows the source asset), Add Payload (a reference that loads on demand) or Add Copy (an independent copy).
The Asset Browser on the mobile robots of Sodero Assets
  • For a material, select the object first, then open the browser and choose Bind Material.
  • Upload from PC uploads a single USD file to the browser's Workspace library, from which you add it the same way. For a scene made of several files, use Replace scene… with a zip.
  • Sodero Assets are published by Sodero: you can view, edit and simulate them in Sodero, but exports and downloads leave them out (Libraries).

docs.title: 3. Arrange and Edit
docs.text:
Select an object in the viewport or in the Hierarchy. The viewport outlines it, and Asset detail shows its properties.

The jackal selected in the Hierarchy and in the viewport
  • Move, rotate and scale. Pick Select, Move, Rotate or Scale at the bottom of the viewport and drag the gizmo; Snap turns snapping on and off. Or type Position, Rotation (degrees) and Scale under Transform. A field applies when you press Enter or leave it.
  • Organize. + in the Scene panel adds a Group or a light; a World without lights looks dark. Right-click a row for Focus, Show or Hide, Lock or Unlock, Rename, Duplicate, Delete and more. Drag a row onto another to move it under that object.
  • Physics. Set the Mass (kg) or the Density (kg/m³) of the selected body.
  • Joints. For a robot, Joints lists its movable joints in alphabetical order, for example Joints (4) for the Jackal. Pose a joint with − and + (5° or 5 cm per step) or type a value. Reset pose sets every joint back to zero.

Studio has no tools to create articulations, joints, colliders or cameras: prepare robots before you bring them in (Prepare a World for Simulation).

docs.title: 4. Save, Revisions and Export
docs.text:
Action How What happens Save Save now in the left rail, or World › Save now Writes the World to its files in the project. The header shows Saved just now. Autosave World › Autosave › 5, 10, 15 or 30 min Saves at that interval, every 10 minutes by default Revisions World › Show Revisions… Create Revision saves the World and keeps a copy. A revision's ⋯ menu offers Restore this revision and Delete. Export World › Export Downloads the World: one .usd file, or a zip when the World uses other files
  • Activating a World loads its last saved state, so save before you activate. If the World is active while you save, the running World is updated.
  • Restoring a revision first keeps the current state as a revision.
  • A World whose scene Sodero provides cannot be exported. When a World uses Sodero Assets, the export leaves those files out and says how many.

docs.title: 5. Work Together
docs.text:
• Everyone who opens the same World in Studio joins one editing session and sees the others' changes. The header shows who is there.
  • Selecting an object reserves it for you: the others see who has it and cannot change it until you select something else.
  • Save now and Replace scene… act on everyone's changes in the session.
  • People with Can view see a View only badge. They can look around and inspect objects, but not change the World.

docs.title: 6. Keys and Camera
docs.text:
Input Action Q, W, E, R Select, Move, Rotate, Scale tool N Snap on or off F Frame the selection, or the whole World when nothing is selected Shift+F, Esc Follow the selection; stop following Right-drag Look around Right-drag with W A S D Q E Fly forward, left, back, right, down and up; Shift flies faster, the wheel changes the speed Wheel, or Alt + right-drag Move closer or farther Middle-drag Pan Alt + left-drag Orbit

The keys are ignored while you type in a field.

docs.title: 7. Enter Theater
docs.text:
Click Enter Theater ▾ in the header and choose RTX Real-time or WebGPU. Studio activates the World if needed, which can take a minute, and opens it in Theater in a new tab. Once the World is active, the button reads Open Theater.

If another World of the project is active, Studio says Another World is already running: click Open running World to watch that one, or Cancel.

An active World uses credits. Enter Theater activates the World. Deactivate it on the project page when you are done (Activate and Run).

docs.title: Theater
docs.text: Theater shows an active Robot World live in your browser: the simulation as it runs, the robots in it and the Stations that drive them. Its browser tab is titled Cosmic Theater.

docs.title: 1. Open Theater
docs.text:
1. Activate the World on the project page (Activate and Run).
  2. Click Theater in the World's Actions column. The link is available once the World is Active and its live view is ready.

  3. In Choose rendering mode, pick RTX Real-time or WebGPU and click Open Cosmic Theater (Choose Rendering Mode). Theater opens in a new tab.

  4. From Studio, Enter Theater activates the World if needed and opens it here (Studio).

  5. While the World loads, Theater shows the progress, including Robot cameras when the World has cameras. The first time a scene opens in RTX Real-time, the renderer prepares it, which can take several minutes.
  6. Opening Theater does not play the World: Run on the project page or Start Theater plays it (Start and Stop).
  7. Watching counts as use of the World: an active World that nobody watches in Theater is deactivated by Auto off after 30 minutes.

docs.title: 2. The Theater Window
docs.text:
Area What it holds Header The project and World names; the status, Ready once the World is shown; the renderer menu (RTX Real-time ▾ or WebGPU ▾); a timer; Start Theater or Stop Theater; Resources ▾; Share (link icon); the Active users who are watching Scene assets The top levels of the World, with Search assets and the number of assets. Hide panel folds it away. Viewport The running World. Perspective ▾ holds camera presets (Perspective, Top, Bottom, Front, Back, Left, Right). View ▾ holds Grid, Quality (resolution and frame rate), Fit and Presentation mode, which shows the viewport full screen until you press Esc. Readout At the bottom of the viewport, for example 1920x1080 · 60 FPS · Physics RTF 1.00 Runtime The Station that drives the selected robot (Select a Robot)

Physics RTF is the real-time factor of the simulation: simulated time divided by wall-clock time, measured over about five seconds. At 1.00 the simulation keeps up with real time; — means there is no fresh measurement. FPS is the rate at which the picture is drawn.

The renderer menu switches your view to the other rendering mode. The current picture stays until the new one is ready. The choice applies to your view only; the simulation is the same for everyone.

docs.title: Start and Stop
docs.text:
Start Theater plays the World's simulation and Stop Theater stops it. One viewer controls them: the first person with edit access who opened Theater. For the others, the button is dimmed and they watch. Members with Can view always watch. While the World is not playing, viewers who watch see the status Ready · Paused.

Theater plays and stops only the simulation; it does not start or stop any Station. Run and Stop on the project page act on the files you select there, the World and its Stations alike (Activate and Run).

docs.title: 3. Move the Camera
docs.text:
The camera moves as in Studio: right-drag to look around, the wheel to move closer or farther, middle-drag to pan and Alt + left-drag to orbit (Keys and Camera). Each viewer has their own camera.

Key Action F Frame the selection, or the whole World when nothing is selected Shift+F Follow the selection. A Tracking chip appears; Stop on it ends the tracking. Esc Stop following; leave presentation mode

Right-click a row in Scene assets for Focus and Focus and Track.

docs.title: 4. Select a Robot
docs.text:
1. Click a robot in the viewport, or its row in Scene assets. Double-click the row to bring the camera to the robot.
  2. In RTX Real-time, a card appears above the robot with its name and Open Station, followed by the Robot System that drives it. In both modes, right-clicking the robot's row in Scene assets offers Open Station as well.
  3. Open Station opens that Robot System's live Station in a new tab. Members with Can view get a page they can only look at.

The Runtime dock opens on the right by itself when you select a robot that a Station drives. It shows that Station's graph, read-only, with the state of each node, so you can see at a glance whether the gateway and the controller are running.

  • Widen Runtime makes the dock wider, and Hide Runtime closes it. Show Runtime in a row's right-click menu opens it again.
  • The zoom buttons and Fit view at the bottom arrange the graph.
  • When no Station drives the robot, the card or the menu says so, for example No Station is running in this project.

docs.title: 5. Several Viewers
docs.text:
• Everyone who opens an active World watches the same simulation. Active users in the header shows who is watching.
  • Each person chooses their own rendering mode and moves their own camera.
  • Each viewer in RTX Real-time has a cloud renderer of their own, which uses credits. A viewer in WebGPU draws with their own computer's GPU, and your plan may still count that view (Billing and Usage).
  • Share shows the link to this Theater, and Copy copies it. The link opens for people who are signed in and have access to the project (Share and Collaborate).

docs.title: 6. What Theater Does Not Do
docs.text:
• It does not edit the World. Deactivate the World and open it in Studio.
  • It does not start or stop Stations; use Run and Stop on the project page, or the Station itself.
  • It has no recording or screenshot button. To capture the view, use your operating system's screenshot or screen-recording tools.
